Optics also writes `junit_output.xml` when you stop the run with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. The test case in progress ends as `ERROR`, with the code E0706. The test cases that did not start are `NOT_RUN`. Suite Teardown does not run.

On-screen errors found by error detection appear in `junit_output.xml` as a failing test case. They count as a failed test case, so the exit code is 1.

```shell
$ optics execute ./birch-tests
$ OPTICS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1 optics execute ./birch-tests --no-use-printer
```

## `optics live`

Opens an interactive session where you type keywords, see each result straight away, and save what worked as a test.

```text
optics live [folder]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | Current folder | The project folder. It must contain a config.yaml. |

The config must enable exactly one driver and at least one element source. Without a config, `optics live` stops with an error; there are no built-in defaults. Live runs `launch_app` as soon as it starts.

Type a keyword with its parameters, for example `press_element ${sign_in}` or `enter_text ${email_field} "ana@birch.example"`. Each result appears as two lines:

```terminal
  ✓ press_element ${sign_in}
     0.31s  [XPath]
```

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/save <test_case> <module>` | Saves the steps you've run since the last save as a module and a test case in CSV. Names can't contain spaces. |
| `/device [id]` | Lists connected Android and iOS devices, or switches to one. Appium only. |
| `/elements` | Shows the named elements in the project. |
| `/screenshot` | Saves a screenshot to `screenshots/` in the project. |
| `/help` | Shows help. |
| `/quit`, `/exit` | Quits. Warns once if you have unsaved steps. |

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Completes keyword names. |
| `${` | Suggests element names. |
| Ctrl+K | Opens the keyword browser. |
| Ctrl+N | Switches to plain-English mode. Needs an enabled `llm_models` entry. Tune it with [`nl_agent`](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#nl-agent). |
| Ctrl+X | Stops a running plain-English instruction. |
| Ctrl+C | Quits. |

Live writes its log to `logs/optics_live_<time>.log` and its screenshots to `screenshots/session_<time>/` in the project. See [Record a test](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/record) for a full walkthrough.

## `optics serve`

Starts the HTTP API so any language or tool can drive a device through Optics.

```text
optics serve [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--workers N]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. |
| `--port` | `8000` | The port to listen on. |
| `--workers` | `1` | Server processes. Keep it at 1: sessions live in memory and aren't shared between processes. |

**Warning:**
The API has no authentication. Keep the default `127.0.0.1`, unless you are on a trusted network. On another address, the server logs a warning when it starts.

Web pages cannot call the server unless you list their origins in `OPTICS_CORS_ORIGINS`. A request whose `Host` is not a loopback name gets `421`. Add other names in `OPTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

The server doesn't read config.yaml. Each session gets its settings from the request. Interactive API docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`. See [HTTP API](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/http-api).

```shell
$ optics serve --port 8000
```

## `optics mcp`

Starts the MCP server, which lets an AI agent such as Claude or Cursor drive a device with Optics keywords.

```text
optics mcp [--transport stdio|http] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--toolset core|full]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--transport` | `stdio` | `stdio` for agents that start the server themselves; `http` to serve at `http://<host>:<port>/mcp`. |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. `http` only. |
| `--port` | `8090` | The port to listen on. `http` only. |
| `--toolset` | `core`, or `OPTICS_MCP_TOOLSET` | `core` gives the agent a small set of tools. `full` also adds one tool for each keyword. |

It needs the `mcp` extra, which the install scripts include. With pip: `pip install "optics-framework[mcp]"`. The `all` bundle doesn't include it. Without the extra, the command exits with code 1 and prints the install command. See [MCP server](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp).

## `optics generate`

Turns a CSV or YAML project into pytest or Robot Framework code.

```text
optics generate <folder> [--framework pytest|robot] [--output FILE]
```

| Argument | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | Required | The project folder. |
| `--framework` | `pytest` | `pytest` or `robot`. |
| `--output` | `test_generated.py` or `test_generated.robot` | A file name, not a path. The file always goes in `<folder>/generated/Tests/`. |

It writes:

- `generated/Tests/<file>`: the generated tests.
- `generated/requirements.txt`: the packages the generated code needs.
- `generated/Tests/input_templates/`: a copy of `input_templates/` if that folder sits at the project root.

Generate has stricter needs than `optics execute`:

- The config file must be named exactly `config.yaml`.
- The project needs an elements file. Only the `Element_ID` column is used; fallback columns are ignored.
- Every `${name}` must come from the elements file. Run a suite that sets values with Evaluate, Date Evaluate or `store_as` with `optics execute`.
- Flow-control keywords (`Run Loop`, `Condition`, `Evaluate` and the rest) and a few others are skipped without a warning.
- Suite Setup and Suite Teardown become ordinary tests.

Exit code 3 if a required file is missing or two files define the same name. See [Generate code](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/generate).

```shell
$ optics generate ./birch-tests --framework robot --output smoke.robot
```

## `optics list`

Prints every keyword you can use, grouped by category.

```text
optics list
```

Names are printed in snake_case. In a module, write them in Title Case with spaces: `press_element` becomes `Press Element`. Matching ignores case and spaces, so both forms work.

```terminal
ActionKeyword:
  - clear_element_text
  - detect_and_press
  ...
AppManagement:
  - launch_app
  ...
```

For parameters and examples, see [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/).

## `optics completion`

Turns on tab completion for `optics` in bash or zsh.

```text
optics completion
```

It writes `~/.optics/optics_completion.sh` and `~/.optics/optics_completion.zsh`, then asks before it adds a `# Optics CLI autocompletion` comment and a `source` line to `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`, based on `$SHELL`. If you decline, or the terminal is not interactive, Optics leaves the file alone and prints the line to add. Other shells are not supported. Restart your shell, or run `source ~/.zshrc`, to use it. To remove it, delete the comment and the `source` line from your shell profile.

## `optics config`

Deprecated. Use [`optics configure`](#optics-configure).

```text
optics config
```

It prints a deprecation notice, then runs guided `optics configure` on the current folder. There's no global config file any more: every setting lives in the project's config.yaml.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success. For `optics execute` and `optics dry_run`, every test case passed. |
| `1` | A test case failed, error detection found an on-screen error, a check failed (`optics doctor --check`, preflight), a required file or setting is missing, or an unexpected error occurred. |
| `2` | The command line was invalid, for example an unknown flag or a missing argument. |
| `3` | The input was invalid. For `optics execute` and `optics dry_run`, a name in `--include`, `--exclude` or the config `include` and `exclude` matches no test case, or no test case is left. For other commands, it is a project that already exists, an unknown template, or files `optics generate` needs. The message starts with `Error:`. |
| `130` | You pressed Ctrl+C. Optics prints `Operation cancelled by user.` |
| `143` | Optics received SIGTERM. `optics execute` and `optics dry_run` write `junit_output.xml` before they exit. |

## Environment variables

None of these override config.yaml. Settings for `optics execute`, `dry_run` and `live` come only from the project's config.yaml.

| Variable | Used by | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OPTICS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT` | `execute` | Set to `1` or `true` to skip the server and device check before a run. |
| `OPTICS_HOME` | `optics` | Folder for the first-run marker. Default `~/.optics`. |
| `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL` | `serve`, `mcp` | Set to `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` to turn on AI self-heal for every session by default. |
| `OPTICS_LLM_PROVIDER` | `serve`, `mcp` | The LLM engine for self-heal: `gemini` (default), `openai` or `anthropic`. |
| `OPTICS_LLM_MODEL` | `serve`, `mcp` | The model for self-heal. Gemini defaults to `gemini-2.5-flash`; `openai` and `anthropic` need one. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_ALLOW_COORDINATE_TAPS` | `mcp` | Set to `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` to let the agent use `press_by_coordinates`, `press_by_percentage` and `swipe`. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_TOOLSET` | `mcp` | The default for `--toolset`: `core` or `full`. Any other value stops the server. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_SESSION_IDLE_S` | `mcp` | Seconds before an unused session ends. Default `900`. `0` keeps sessions open. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT_S` | `mcp` | Seconds that one tool call can take. Default `100`. |
| `OPTICS_CORS_ORIGINS` | `serve` | Web origins that can call the server, separated by commas. Empty by default, so no web page can call it. `*` stops the server with E0501. |
| `OPTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | `serve`, `mcp` over HTTP | Host names that the server answers in addition to loopback names, separated by commas. When set, the check applies on any address. Other hosts get `421`. |
| `OPTICS_EVENT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S` | `execute`, `serve` | Seconds to wait for events to flush at the end of a run. Default `2.0`. Raise it if `junit_output.xml` is cut short on long runs. |
| `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` | `doctor`, Playwright | Where Playwright browsers are installed. |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Gemini | API key for the Gemini Developer API. `capabilities.api_key` in config.yaml wins over it. |
| `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | Gemini, Google Vision | Use Vertex AI and Google Cloud credentials instead of an API key. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `openai` engine | API key for OpenAI. `capabilities.api_key` in config.yaml wins over it. Set `api_key_env` to read another variable. |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `openai` engine | The server to call when the entry has no `url`, such as OpenRouter or a local Ollama. |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `anthropic` engine | API key for the Claude API. `capabilities.api_key` in config.yaml wins over it. Set `api_key_env` to read another variable. |
| Any name in `${NAME}` | Playwright | A `${NAME}` in the Playwright `url` or in a `headers` value is read from the environment. If it is not set, the run stops with [E0501](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e05-files-and-config). |

`Read Data` can also read any variable with `ENV:<NAME>` in a project run. `optics serve` and `optics mcp` refuse `ENV:`. `optics serve` and `optics mcp` over HTTP also refuse a `Read Data` file. See [Flow control keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/flow).

## Install scripts

The install scripts put Optics in its own virtual environment under `~/.optics` and add the `optics` command to your PATH. They don't change your system Python. Python 3.12 or later is the one prerequisite.

**macOS and Linux**

```shell
$ curl -fsSL https://optics-framework.org/install | sh
```

Pass options after `sh -s --`:

```shell
$ curl -fsSL https://optics-framework.org/install | sh -s -- --extra appium,easyocr
```

| Option | Environment variable | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--version X.Y.Z` | `OPTICS_VERSION` | Installs a specific release. |
| `--extra a,b` | | Also installs engine extras, for example `appium,llm`. The `mcp` extra is always installed. |
| `--dir PATH` | `OPTICS_INSTALL_DIR` | Installs somewhere other than `~/.optics`. |
| `--no-modify-path` | `OPTICS_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | Leaves your shell profile alone. |
| `--dry-run` | | Prints what would happen and changes nothing. |
| `--uninstall` | | Removes Optics and the PATH line it added to your shell profile. Other files in the folder are kept. |
| `--help` | | Shows the options. |

On Windows under Git Bash, MSYS2 or Cygwin, the script stops and points you to the PowerShell installer. Inside WSL, use this script.
**Windows**

```powershell
PS> irm https://optics-framework.org/install.ps1 | iex
```

Piping into `iex` can't pass parameters, so set environment variables first:

```powershell
PS> $env:OPTICS_EXTRA = "appium,easyocr"
PS> irm https://optics-framework.org/install.ps1 | iex
```

| Parameter (downloaded script) | Environment variable | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `-Version X.Y.Z` | `OPTICS_VERSION` | Installs a specific release. |
| `-Extra a,b` | `OPTICS_EXTRA` | Also installs engine extras. The `mcp` extra is always installed. |
| `-Dir PATH` | `OPTICS_INSTALL_DIR` | Installs somewhere other than `~\.optics`. |
| `-NoModifyPath` | `OPTICS_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | Leaves your PATH alone. |
| `-DryRun` | | Prints what would happen and changes nothing. |
| `-Uninstall` | | Removes Optics and its entry in your user PATH. Other files in the folder are kept. |

To pass parameters without downloading the script, run it as a script block:

```powershell
PS> & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://optics-framework.org/install.ps1))) -Uninstall
```
**pip**

```shell
$ python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
$ pip install "optics-framework[appium,easyocr]"
```

Install into a virtual environment you control. Add [extras](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines) in the brackets.

See [Install Optics](https://optics-framework.org/docs/get-started/install) for a step-by-step guide.

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config

# config.yaml

> Every setting in a project's config.yaml.

A project's config.yaml tells Optics which driver to use, how to find elements, and where to write logs and results. Every setting lives in the project; there's no global config file and no environment variable that overrides it.

Run [`optics configure`](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#optics-configure) to write a working file by answering a few questions, then edit it by hand with this page.

## How Optics finds the file

| Command | Which file it reads |
|---|---|
| `optics execute`, `optics dry_run` | Any YAML file in the project tree that has `driver_sources` and `elements_sources`. The file name doesn't matter. If there are several, the last one found wins. |
| `optics live` | The first YAML file in the project tree with any config key. |
| `optics doctor`, `optics configure`, `optics generate` | Exactly `<folder>/config.yaml`. |
| `optics serve`, `optics mcp` | None. Settings come from each session request. |

We recommend one file named `config.yaml` at the project root, so every command reads the same settings.

Settings you leave out take their defaults. Optics ignores keys it doesn't know, so a typo such as `log_levle` is silently skipped.

**Warning:**
If config.yaml has a wrong value type, `optics execute` logs the problem, skips the file and runs with defaults. The run then stops with "No driver enabled". Run `optics doctor <folder>` to find the problem.

## Top-level keys

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `driver_sources` | All disabled | The driver that controls the device or browser. See [driver_sources](#driver-sources). |
| `elements_sources` | All disabled | Where Optics looks for elements: the driver's UI tree, its locators, or its screenshots. `element_sources` is accepted as an alias in each command, `optics doctor` included. If the file has both keys, Optics uses `elements_sources`. |
| `text_detection` | All disabled | OCR engines for finding elements by on-screen text. |
| `image_detection` | All disabled | Engines for finding elements by image templates. |
| `llm_models` | All disabled | The LLM for AI self-heal and the plain-English mode of `optics live`. |
| `nl_agent` | See [nl_agent](#nl-agent) | Settings for the plain-English mode of `optics live`. |
| `log_level` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR` or `CRITICAL`, any case. Unknown values become `INFO`. |
| `file_log` | `false` | Writes `internal_logs.log` and `execution_logs.log` to the output folder. |
| `log_path` | None | One file for both logs instead of two. Used only with `file_log: true`. |
| `json_log` | `false` | Writes a JSON array of every test, module and keyword event to `logs.json` at the end of the run. |
| `json_path` | None | Where to write the JSON events instead of `<output>/logs.json`. `~` is expanded. |
| `console` | `true` | **Has no effect.** Nothing reads it. Use `log_level` to control console output. |
| `execution_output_path` | `<project>/execution_output` | Where results, screenshots and logs go. A path that starts with `./` or `../` is relative to the project folder. Other relative paths are relative to the folder you run `optics` from. |
| `include` | None | Run only these test cases. See [include and exclude](#include-and-exclude). |
| `exclude` | None | Skip these test cases. |
| `ai_self_heal` | `false` | Lets an LLM try to recover when an element can't be found. See [ai_self_heal](#ai-self-heal). |
| `strict_element_match` | `false` | Turns off fuzzy and partial text matching. See [strict_element_match](#strict-element-match). |
| `save_captures` | `true` | Whether Optics writes screenshots of steps and captures. See [save_captures](#save-captures). |
| `halt_duration` | `0.1` | Seconds to wait after a keyword fails every fallback. It isn't a pause between steps. |
| `event_attributes_json` | None | Path to a JSON file of event attributes. When it includes an `eventUrl`, events you label with `event_name` are sent there at the end of the session. |
| `project_path` | The project folder | The CLI always sets this to the folder you pass, so leave it out. It only matters for the Python SDK. |

**Note:**
If you set `execution_output_path` yourself, create the folder first. This applies to a `./` path too. JUnit results and logs create their own folders, but screenshots fail to save without a warning if the folder is missing.

## Use environment variables and project paths

Any text value in config.yaml can name an environment variable or a file in the project. Use this to keep secrets out of the file, and to keep a project runnable after you copy it to another computer. Optics resolves each reference when it reads the file.

| Write | Optics uses |
|---|---|
| `$NAME` or `${NAME}` | The value of `NAME`. If `NAME` is not set or is empty, the command stops with [E0501](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e05-files-and-config). |
| `${NAME:-default}` | The value of `NAME`, or `default` when `NAME` is not set or is empty. |
| `$$` | A literal `$`. |
| `./file` or `../file` | The full path of the file, counted from the project folder and not from the folder you run `optics` in. |

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - playwright:
      enabled: true
      capabilities:
        $from: $PW_CAPS
        viewport: {width: 800, height: 600}
        storage_state: ./auth.json
execution_output_path: ./out/run2
log_level: ${LEVEL:-INFO}
```

- A reference can be part of a longer string, for example `https://${HUB_HOST}/wd/hub`.
- A variable can hold a `./` path. Optics resolves it in the same way.
- A `./` path must point to a file or folder that exists. The output paths `execution_output_path`, `log_path`, `json_path` and `project_path` do not need to exist.
- The result is always a string. Optics converts it for its own settings, such as `enabled`, `file_log` and `halt_duration`. A driver capability that needs a number or a boolean gets the text. For example, `headless: ${HEADLESS:-true}` fails on Playwright with `headless: expected boolean, got string`. Use `$from` for such values.

To take a whole map from one variable, write `$from` in the map and set the variable to a JSON object. The keys next to `$from` replace the keys of the object. Optics does not resolve references or paths inside the object, and the JSON types stay as they are:

```shell
$ export PW_CAPS='{"browser": "chromium", "headless": true, "viewport": {"width": 100, "height": 100}}'
```

With this variable, the example above starts Chromium without a window and with an 800 x 600 page.

If a reference or path fails, the command stops before the first test and names the problem. These are the messages that `optics execute` and `optics doctor` show:

```terminal
The config uses $LEVEL, but the LEVEL environment variable is not set or is empty.
The config refers to ./missing.json, but /home/ava/birch-tests/missing.json does not exist.
The config takes $from: $PW_CAPS, but its value is not a JSON object.
```

The last message does not show the value of the variable.

**Note:**
The commands `optics execute`, `optics dry_run`, `optics live` and `optics doctor` resolve references. The Python SDK, `optics serve` and `optics mcp` take the settings as data and resolve nothing. `optics configure --edit` keeps references as you wrote them when it saves the file.

A Playwright `url` and `capabilities.headers` are the exception. The driver resolves them when it connects, so it can mask the values in its errors. An unset variable in them still stops the command when it reads the file. Do not use `$from` in `headers`. Write each header on its own line.

## Engine lists

`driver_sources`, `elements_sources`, `text_detection`, `image_detection` and `llm_models` are lists. Each item is an engine name with its settings:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:                 # engine name
      enabled: true         # required: only enabled entries are loaded
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:4723"
      capabilities:         # engine-specific settings
        platformName: Android
```

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | Required | Only enabled entries are loaded. A disabled entry with any name is ignored. |
| `url` | None | The server address, for engines that use one. |
| `capabilities` | `{}` | Settings passed to the engine. |

When several entries in one list are enabled, Optics tries them in the order you list them. For element sources this is the order in which strategies run.

An enabled entry with an unknown name fails with [E0601](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e06-modules-and-engines). So does an enabled engine whose extra isn't installed. A list you write replaces the default list completely.

### driver_sources

Enable one driver. `optics live` refuses more than one, and `optics doctor` warns about it.

| Name | Extra | What it drives |
|---|---|---|
| `appium` | `appium` | Android, iOS, Android TV, Samsung Tizen TV and LG webOS TV apps through an Appium server. |
| `selenium` | `selenium` | Chrome or Firefox through a Selenium server or Grid. |
| `playwright` | `playwright` | Chromium, Firefox or WebKit, on this computer or a remote browser. See [Playwright capabilities](#playwright-capabilities). |
| `ble` | `ble` | Any device paired with a Bluetooth mouse-and-keyboard dongle. For devices with no automation access. |

### elements_sources

Enable the sources that match your driver. We recommend the locator, page source and screenshot sources for your driver. With Appium, add `appium_web` to find elements in web pages.

| Name | Needs driver | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| `appium_find_element` | `appium` | Finds elements by XPath, accessibility id and class. |
| `appium_page_source` | `appium` | Searches the UI tree by XPath and text, with fuzzy matching. Lists interactive elements. |
| `appium_screenshot` | `appium` | Screenshots for OCR, image matching and AI self-heal. |
| `appium_web` | `appium` | Finds `css=` and DOM XPath locators in Chrome and WebViews on Android, and in Safari and WebViews on iOS. Lists the page's interactive elements. It does not tap an element that another element covers. See [Test mobile websites](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/mobile-web). |
| `selenium_find_element` | `selenium` | Finds elements by XPath, text, id, name, CSS and link text. |
| `selenium_page_source` | `selenium` | Searches the page HTML. Doesn't list interactive elements. |
| `selenium_screenshot` | `selenium` | Screenshots for OCR and image matching. |
| `playwright_find_element` | `playwright` | Finds elements by `xpath=`, `css=`, `text=`, `label=`, `placeholder=`, `role=`, `id=`, `data-testid=`, `data-test=` and `data-test-id=` locators. A value with no prefix is tried as text, label, placeholder, button name and link name. |
| `playwright_page_source` | `playwright` | Searches the page and lists interactive elements. |
| `playwright_screenshot` | `playwright` | Screenshots for OCR and image matching. |
| `camera_screenshot` | Any | Frames from a webcam, an HTTP(S) screenshot URL or a TCP frame server. Used with `ble`, or after the screenshot source of a driver for screens that the driver cannot capture. |

`optics doctor` fails a project when no enabled element source starts with the enabled driver's name.

### text_detection

| Name | Extra | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| `easyocr` | `easyocr` | None. Accurate but slow on CPU. Downloads its models on first use. The language is always English. |
| `pytesseract` | `pytesseract` | None. Needs the Tesseract program installed and on your PATH. |
| `google_vision` | `google-vision` | `capabilities.api_key`: a Cloud Vision API key, or `capabilities.credentials_path`: a service account key file. Set only one: both stop the run with E0501. Without them, Optics uses Application Default Credentials, such as `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. `googlevision` also works. |
| `remote_ocr` | None | `url` (required): your OCR service. `capabilities`: `timeout` (30), `method` (`easyocr`), `language` (`en`). Optics posts screenshots to `<url>/detect-text`. |

### image_detection

| Name | Extra | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| `templatematch` | None | `capabilities.sift_nfeatures` (2000). Finds template images, including scaled or rotated ones. Images are found by file name anywhere in the project. |
| `remote_oir` | None | `url` (required): your image service. `capabilities`: `timeout` (30), `method` (`template_matching`). Optics posts to `<url>/detect-image`. |

### llm_models

Optics supports three LLM engines: `gemini`, `openai` and `anthropic`. Each has an extra of the same name, and the `llm` bundle installs all three. If you enable more than one entry, Optics tries them in list order and moves to the next when a call fails.

Each engine reads its API key from `capabilities.api_key` first, then from an environment variable. To keep the key out of the file, write a reference such as `api_key: ${GEMINI_API_KEY}`. Optics reads the variable when it loads the file. If the variable is not set, the run stops with [E0501](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e05-files-and-config) before it starts. Logs and reports show `****` in place of the key.

Each engine also takes `timeout_s` under `capabilities`: the seconds that one request can take, default `60`. A value that is not a positive number fails with [E0601](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e06-modules-and-engines).

#### gemini

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `gemini-2.5-flash` | The Gemini model. |
| `use_vertexai` | From `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI` | `true` uses Vertex AI instead of the Gemini API. |
| `project`, `location` | From `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` | The Vertex AI project and region. |
| `temperature` | The model's default | Sampling temperature. |
| `credentials_path` | None | A Vertex AI service account key file. It selects Vertex AI and sets the project to the `project_id` of the key. |
| `api_key` | None | The Gemini API key, or a reference such as `${GEMINI_API_KEY}`. `gemini_api_key` also works. |

```yaml
llm_models:
  - gemini:
      enabled: true
      capabilities:
        model: gemini-2.5-flash
```

Without `api_key`, Gemini reads its key from `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. For Vertex AI, set `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true` with `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. The key does not select the backend. If `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI` selects Vertex AI and you want the Gemini API, also set `use_vertexai: false`.

To use a service account key file, set `credentials_path` and leave out the API key:

```yaml
llm_models:
  - gemini:
      enabled: true
      capabilities:
        credentials_path: ./credentials/vertex.json
        location: us-east4
```

`credentials_path` selects Vertex AI. The project is the `project_id` of the key, unless you set `project`. The location is `global`, unless you set `location`. If the file is missing or is not a service account key, Optics stops with E0501. This happens before the first test when `ai_self_heal` is `true`.

#### openai

Works with OpenAI and any server that offers an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API. Set the entry's `url` to the server's base URL, or leave it out to call OpenAI. `OPENAI_BASE_URL` works in place of `url`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | None (required) | The model name as the server spells it, for example `gpt-5-mini`, or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` on OpenRouter. |
| `api_key` | None | The key, or a reference such as `${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}`. Optics uses it before `api_key_env`. |
| `api_key_env` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | The environment variable that holds the key. |
| `response_format` | `json_schema` | Set `json_object` if the server rejects JSON-schema output. Optics then puts the schema in the prompt instead. |
| `max_tokens` | The server's limit | The longest reply the model may write. |
| `temperature` | The model's default | Sampling temperature. |

| Server | `url` | Key |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI | Leave it out | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| OpenRouter | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `api_key: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}` |
| Azure OpenAI | `https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/` | Your Azure key, in `api_key` |
| Ollama | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | None |
| vLLM, LM Studio | The server's `/v1` URL | None |

```yaml
llm_models:
  - openai:
      enabled: true
      url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
      capabilities:
        model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
        api_key: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}
```

With no key and no `url`, the engine stops with [E0601](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e06-modules-and-engines): "found no API key: set capabilities.api_key or OPENAI_API_KEY". A server at a `url` can work without a key.

#### anthropic

Use Claude through the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI. For Bedrock or Vertex AI, also install `anthropic[bedrock]` or `anthropic[vertex]` into the same Python environment as Optics.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | None (required) | The model ID, for example `claude-sonnet-5-5`. Bedrock and Vertex AI use their own model IDs. |
| `platform` | `anthropic` | `anthropic` (the Claude API), `bedrock` or `vertex`. |
| `region` | From the environment | The Bedrock or Vertex AI region. |
| `project` | From the environment | The Vertex AI project. |
| `api_key` | None | The Claude API key, or a reference such as `${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}`. Only for `platform: anthropic`. Optics uses it before `api_key_env`. |
| `api_key_env` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | The environment variable that holds the Claude API key. Only for `platform: anthropic`. |
| `max_tokens` | `4096` | The longest reply the model may write. |
| `temperature` | The model's default | Sampling temperature. |

| Platform | Credentials |
|---|---|
| `anthropic` | `api_key`, else `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or the variable `api_key_env` names |
| `bedrock` | Your usual AWS credentials, such as `AWS_PROFILE` and `AWS_REGION` |
| `vertex` | Google Cloud application default credentials |

The entry's `url`, if you set it, replaces the API address on all three platforms.

### nl_agent

Settings for the plain-English mode of `optics live`. They apply only when an `llm_models` entry is enabled.

```yaml
nl_agent:
  vision: auto
  max_steps: 15
  escalation_model: ""
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `vision` | `auto` | When Optics sends a screenshot with the screen elements. `auto` sends one when the element list is not sufficient, for example after a failed step. `always` and `never` do what they say. |
| `max_steps` | `15` | The maximum number of steps for one instruction. It must be 1 or more. |
| `escalation_model` | `""` | A stronger model for difficult steps, such as a retry after a failure. It uses the engine of the first enabled `llm_models` entry. Empty uses the same model for all steps. |

## Examples by platform

**Android**

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:4723"        # required; the Appium server
      capabilities:                        # must not be empty
        platformName: Android              # required; picks the Android profile
        automationName: UiAutomator2
        deviceName: emulator-5554
        # udid: emulator-5554              # pin one device when several are connected
        appPackage: com.birch.shop         # the app Launch App opens
        appActivity: com.birch.shop.MainActivity
elements_sources:
  - appium_find_element: {enabled: true}   # XPath, accessibility id, class
  - appium_page_source:  {enabled: true}   # UI tree search (uses strict_element_match)
  - appium_screenshot:   {enabled: true}   # screenshots for OCR, images, self-heal
text_detection:
  - easyocr: {enabled: true}               # extra: easyocr
image_detection:
  - templatematch: {enabled: true}
log_level: INFO
file_log: true
json_log: true
```

Before `optics execute`, Optics checks that the Appium server answers. If the server is on this computer, it also checks that `adb devices` lists a device.
**iOS**

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://127.0.0.1:4723"
      capabilities:
        platformName: iOS                  # picks the iOS profile
        automationName: XCUITest
        deviceName: "iPhone 15"
        bundleId: com.birch.shop           # required on iOS
        # udid: <device udid>              # for a real device
elements_sources:
  - appium_find_element: {enabled: true}
  - appium_page_source:  {enabled: true}
  - appium_screenshot:   {enabled: true}
log_level: INFO
file_log: true
```

`optics doctor` fails an iOS project without `bundleId`. The preflight checks only the Appium server.
**Web**

Use Playwright unless you already run a Selenium Grid. It needs no server.

`config.yaml (Playwright)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - playwright:
      enabled: true                        # no url and no server
      capabilities:
        browser: chromium                  # or firefox, webkit
        headless: false                    # true: no window
elements_sources:
  - playwright_find_element: {enabled: true}
  - playwright_page_source:  {enabled: true}
  - playwright_screenshot:   {enabled: true}
log_level: INFO
```

Open your site with a module step such as `Launch App,https://birch.example`.

`config.yaml (Selenium)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - selenium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://localhost:4444/wd/hub"  # the Selenium server or Grid
      capabilities:                        # must not be empty
        browserName: chrome                # required: chrome or firefox
        browserURL: "https://birch.example"  # opened when the session starts
elements_sources:
  - selenium_find_element: {enabled: true}
  - selenium_page_source:  {enabled: true}
  - selenium_screenshot:   {enabled: true}
log_level: INFO
```

Selenium won't start with empty `capabilities` or without `browserName`. The file `optics configure` writes for `web-selenium` has `capabilities: {}`, so add `browserName` before you run.

Chrome starts with `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` and without the automation switch, so `navigator.webdriver` is `false`. Optics adds no other Chrome argument. In a Linux container or in CI, pass `--no-sandbox` and `--disable-dev-shm-usage` in `goog:chromeOptions`:

`config.yaml (Selenium in a container)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - selenium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://localhost:4444/wd/hub"
      capabilities:
        browserName: chrome
        goog:chromeOptions:
          args: ["--headless=new", "--no-sandbox", "--disable-dev-shm-usage"]
```

Optics sends these arguments with its own. It sends the other keys of `goog:chromeOptions`, such as `excludeSwitches`, to the browser as well.

### Appium capabilities

Optics reads `platformName`, the app id and `browserName`. It passes every other capability to Appium unchanged. You can write any key with the `appium:` prefix, for example `appium:udid`.

| platformName | App id capability | Defaults Optics adds (your values win) |
|---|---|---|
| `Android` | `appPackage` and `appActivity` | `newCommandTimeout: 3600`, `noReset: true`, `forceAppLaunch: true`, `shouldTerminateApp: true`, `nativeWebScreenshot: true`, `connectHardwareKeyboard: true`, `ignoreHiddenApiPolicyError: true` and `settings: {waitForIdleTimeout: 1000}` |
| `iOS` | `bundleId` | The same defaults without `ignoreHiddenApiPolicyError`, with `ensureWebviewsHavePages: true` and `settings: {waitForIdleTimeout: 1}` |
| `TizenTV` | `appPackage` | `newCommandTimeout: 3600`, `rcMode: remote`, `noReset: true` |
| `LGTV` | `appId` | `newCommandTimeout: 600`, `rcMode: rc`, `useSecureWebsocket: true`, `autoExtendDevMode: false`, `noReset: true` |

Any other `platformName` fails with [E0104](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e01-driver-and-session). Optics waits up to 300 seconds for Appium to create a session. To attach to an Appium session that is already running, add `appium:existingSessionId`. Optics starts a new session if it cannot attach.

**Idle wait.** Before each action, Appium waits until the app is idle. `waitForIdleTimeout` sets the limit: 1000 ms on Android and 1 s on iOS. Optics merges your `appium:settings` with its defaults key by key. Set `0` to turn off the wait:

```yaml
capabilities:
  appium:settings:
    waitForIdleTimeout: 0
```

**Web pages.** These defaults let `appium_web` read web pages quickly:

| platformName | Defaults |
|---|---|
| `Android` | `ensureWebviewsHavePages: false`, `extractChromeAndroidPackageFromContextName: true` |
| `iOS` | `includeSafariInWebviews: true`, `additionalWebviewBundleIds: ["*"]`, `webviewConnectRetries: 1`, `webviewAtomWaitTimeout: 5000` |

The iOS defaults apply only to app sessions. With `browserName` or `autoWebview`, the session starts in the browser and Optics leaves them out. See [Test mobile websites](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/mobile-web).

### Playwright capabilities

Optics reads each key from `capabilities` or from the top level of the `playwright` entry. [Web](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web) shows how to use them.

| Capability | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `browser` | `chromium` | `chromium`, `firefox` or `webkit`. `optics setup` downloads only Chromium. |
| `headless` | `false` | `true` starts the browser without a window. A remote browser ignores it. |
| `channel` | None | `chrome`, `chrome-beta` or `msedge`. Starts that installed browser in place of Playwright's Chromium. A remote browser ignores it. |
| `profile` | None | A local Chrome or Edge profile: its directory (`Default`, `Profile 1`), its name or its account email. The run starts with a copy of its sign-ins. Not with `url`, `storage_state` or `user_data_dir`. See [Start signed in with a browser profile](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#start-signed-in-with-a-browser-profile). |
| `user_data_dir` | None | A folder that the browser keeps as its user data directory. Sign-ins stay from run to run. Not with `url`, `storage_state` or `profile`. A path that starts with `./` must exist. |
| `viewport` | `{width: 1280, height: 800}` | The page size. It replaces the screen size of a `device`. |
| `device` | None | A Playwright device name, such as `"iPhone 15"`. It sets the screen size, user agent and touch input. An unknown name fails with [E0501](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e05-files-and-config). See [Emulate a phone](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#emulate-a-phone). |
| `storage_state` | None | A browser state file that Playwright saved, relative to the project folder. The run starts with its cookies and storage. Not with `profile` or `user_data_dir`. See [Start signed in from a saved file](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#start-signed-in-from-a-saved-file). |
| `protocol` | `cdp` | How Optics connects to the browser in `url`: `cdp` (Chromium only) or `playwright`. See [Use a remote browser](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#use-a-remote-browser). |
| `headers` | None | HTTP headers for the connection to a remote browser, as `{name: value}`. |
| `context` | `new` | `existing` uses the remote browser's own context and open tab. You cannot use it with `device` or `storage_state`. |
| `element_timeout_ms` | `10000` | The wait for an element before an action. |
| `navigation_timeout_ms` | `60000` | The limit for a page load from Launch App or Go Back. |
| `navigation_wait_until` | `domcontentloaded` | The load event that a page load waits for: `domcontentloaded`, `load`, `networkidle` or `commit`. |
| `settle_timeout_ms` | `3000` | The wait for the page to stop changes before Optics reads it. `0` turns it off. |
| `connect_timeout_ms` | `90000` | The limit for the connection to a remote browser. |
| `action_timeout_ms` | `15000` | The limit for each other browser call, such as a key press or a screenshot. |

Optics ignores a capability that it does not know and logs a warning. Local Chromium starts without the automation flags, so `navigator.webdriver` is `false`.

Set `url` on the entry to connect to a remote browser instead of starting one. `${NAME}` in `url` or in a `headers` value is read from the environment. If the variable is not set, the run stops with E0501. Sessions that `optics serve` and `optics mcp` start refuse `${NAME}` in `url` and `headers`, a `storage_state` file path and `user_data_dir`. They accept `profile` only from `optics mcp` on stdio.

## TV

Android TV uses the Android example. Samsung and LG TVs use Appium's TV drivers:

`config.yaml (Samsung Tizen)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://localhost:4723"
      capabilities:
        platformName: TizenTV
        appium:automationName: TizenTV
        appium:deviceAddress: 192.168.1.50
        appium:rcToken: "14184553"
        appium:appPackage: com.birch.tv
        appium:app: /path/to/birch.wgt
        appium:chromedriverExecutableDir: /path/to/chromedrivers
elements_sources:
  - appium_find_element: {enabled: true}
```

`config.yaml (LG webOS)`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - appium:
      enabled: true
      url: "http://localhost:4723"
      capabilities:
        platformName: LGTV
        appium:automationName: webOS
        appium:deviceHost: 192.168.1.50
        appium:appId: com.birch.tv
elements_sources:
  - appium_find_element: {enabled: true}
  - appium_screenshot: {enabled: true}
```

On Tizen and webOS, `appium_find_element` finds `text=` and `css=` locators in the app's DOM, and the element keywords press remote keys to move the focus. Touch keywords fail with [E0105](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e01-driver-and-session). A Tizen TV needs `camera_screenshot` in place of `appium_screenshot`. See [Test TV apps](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/tv).

## BLE and camera

The `ble` driver taps and types through a Bluetooth mouse-and-keyboard dongle. A camera or frame server provides the screen, and Optics finds elements with OCR or image templates.

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
driver_sources:
  - ble:
      enabled: true
      capabilities:
        device_id: "Birch test phone"     # required
        port: "/dev/ttyACM0"              # required: device path, COM port or USB product name
        pixel_width: 1080                 # the device screen in pixels
        pixel_height: 2336
        mickeys_width: 1080               # the device screen in mouse units
        mickeys_height: 2336
        x_invert: 1                       # 1 or -1
        y_invert: 1
elements_sources:
  - camera_screenshot:
      enabled: true
      capabilities:
        camera_index: 0                   # a webcam, or url: for a screenshot URL or a TCP frame server
text_detection:
  - easyocr: {enabled: true}
image_detection:
  - templatematch: {enabled: true}
```

| `ble` capability | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `device_id` | Required | A name for the device. |
| `port` | Required | The dongle's serial port (`/dev/ttyACM0`, `COM3`) or its USB product description. |
| `pixel_width`, `pixel_height` | `0` | The device screen size in pixels. Set them: taps can't be placed without them. |
| `mickeys_width`, `mickeys_height` | `0` | The device screen size in mouse movement units. Set them too. |
| `x_invert`, `y_invert` | `1` | `-1` reverses the direction of mouse movement on that axis. |

| `camera_screenshot` capability | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `camera_index` | None | The webcam number. Use this or `url`. |
| `url` | None | An `http://` or `https://` URL that Optics fetches with `GET`, or a TCP frame server as `ip:port`. |
| `token` | None | HTTP only. Optics sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Optics masks it in logs. |
| `header_size` | `8` | TCP only. Bytes in the frame server's length header: `4` or `8`. |
| `byte_order` | `little` | TCP only. The length header's byte order: `little` or `big`. |
| `deskew_corners` | None | The four corners of the screen in the camera frame, as `"x,y"`: top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left. Optics cuts the frame to the screen and makes it straight. |
| `out_width`, `out_height` | `1080`, `1920` | The size of the frame after `deskew_corners`. Set the screenshot size of the device. |
| `rotation` | None | `clockwise` or `counterclockwise`: a quarter turn after `deskew_corners`. |

With an HTTP URL, Optics decodes the body as an image. Any status other than 200 fails with the status and the `code` and `message` of the server's JSON reply. Optics does not follow redirects, because a redirect will send the token again.

If you set neither `url` nor `camera_index`, Optics reads these environment variables. A value in config.yaml wins over a variable.

| Variable | Used for |
|---|---|
| `WEBCAM_SCREENSHOT_URL` | The screenshot URL. |
| `WEBCAM_SCREENSHOT_TOKEN` | The bearer token for `WEBCAM_SCREENSHOT_URL`. Optics sends it to no other URL. |
| `WEBCAM_SCREENSHOT_TCP_PORT` | A TCP frame server at `127.0.0.1` on this port. Optics uses it when `WEBCAM_SCREENSHOT_URL` is not set. |

For a `url` in config.yaml, set `token` too. Keep the token out of the file: `token: ${WEBCAM_SCREENSHOT_TOKEN}`. A `url` with no `token` sends no token, and Optics logs a warning.

Optics checks `deskew_corners` and `rotation` when the session starts. Four points that are not the corners of a convex screen, in order, or another `rotation` value stop the run.

A frame must arrive within 15 seconds. An HTTP reply or a TCP frame larger than 64 MiB fails with [E0304](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e03-screenshots).

The BLE driver can't launch apps, so `Launch App` fails. Open the app by hand or with keys before the run. XPath and text locators don't work without a UI tree; use text that OCR can read, or image templates. See [Test production devices](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/production).

## include and exclude

Run a subset of test cases. The [`--include` and `--exclude` flags](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#pick-test-cases) do the same for one run and replace these keys.

```yaml
include:
  - Shopper can*
exclude:
  - Shopper can check out
```

- A name must match the full `test_case` name. Matching ignores case and extra spaces. `*` and `?` are wildcards.
- You can set both. Optics applies `include` first, then removes the `exclude` matches.
- Each name must match a test case. A name that matches nothing stops the run before it starts, with a suggestion for the name.
- Suite Setup, Suite Teardown and the per-test setup and teardown always run. See [Setup and teardown](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files#setup-and-teardown).

## Logging

| Key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `log_level` | `INFO` | The level for the console and the log files. Set `DEBUG` to see every strategy Optics tries. |
| `file_log` | `false` | Writes `internal_logs.log` and `execution_logs.log` to the output folder. Each rotates at 10 MB and keeps 10 old files. |
| `log_path` | None | Sends both logs to this one file. |
| `json_log` | `false` | Writes `logs.json`: a list of events with name, status, timings and log lines for each test case, module and keyword. |
| `json_path` | None | Writes the JSON events here instead. |
| `console` | `true` | No effect. |

With `file_log: true` and no `execution_output_path`, Optics also writes a copy of both logs to `logs/` in the folder you ran `optics` from.

Optics masks secrets as `****` in the console, the log files, the result tree and the Failure details:

- Values you write with the `@:` prefix, such as `@:s3cret`. After the step runs, Optics also masks the value without the prefix.
- Values that `store_as` or `Read Data` saves under a secret name. A name is secret if it contains one of these words: `pass`, `password`, `passwd`, `passcode`, `pwd`, `pin`, `otp`, `secret`, `token`, `key`, `apikey`, `auth`, `authorization`, `bearer` or `credential`. `password1` and `myAPIToken` are secret names. Optics masks only values of 4 or more characters, also values with `@:`.
- Text values in config.yaml under a secret name, such as `appium:keystorePassword`. Also the values of environment variables with a secret name, such as `HUB_TOKEN`. A key that ends in `_env`, such as `api_key_env`, holds the name of a variable and is not a secret.
- Passwords in URLs (`https://user:****@host`) and query parameters with a secret name (`?token=****`).

Optics also masks secret-named capability values in the debug logs of Appium and Selenium sessions.

See [Read results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results).

## ai_self_heal

When an element can't be found, self-heal sends a screenshot to an LLM and lets it try up to five corrective steps, such as scrolling or closing a popup.

```yaml
ai_self_heal: true
llm_models:
  - gemini:
      enabled: true
```

- It needs an enabled `llm_models` entry, that engine's extra and key, and a screenshot element source such as `appium_screenshot`. Without them it does nothing, and the run isn't affected.
- It applies to keywords that find and act on an element: `Press Element`, `Enter Text`, `Enter Number`, `Clear Element Text`, `Get Text`, `Swipe From Element`, `Scroll From Element`, `Detect And Press` and `Select Dropdown Option`. It doesn't apply to assertions.
- A healed step passes. Check the logs for `AI self-heal:` lines so a real regression doesn't go unnoticed.
- When the step uses `${name}`, Optics sends the element name to the model with the screen. Any engine works, also your own model server with an OpenAI-compatible API. See [Choose a model](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal#choose-a-model).

`optics serve` and `optics mcp` ignore this key. They use per-session fields and the `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL` variable instead. See [Self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal).

## strict_element_match

```yaml
strict_element_match: true
```

By default the page-source element sources (`appium_page_source`, `selenium_page_source`, `playwright_page_source`) accept close or partial text matches, so `Sign in` can match `Sign in with email`. Set `strict_element_match: true` to accept only exact matches. Turn it on when similar labels make tests press the wrong element.

## save_captures

```yaml
save_captures: false
```

When `false`, Optics does not write:

- the files from `Capture Screenshot`, `Capture Pagesource` and `Get Screen Elements`,
- the screenshot before each action, the detection screenshots and the area-of-interest screenshots,
- `failed_steps_elements.json`.

Optics still writes the page source logs and the end-of-run screenshot. `optics serve` always turns captures off.

## Starter config

`optics init` writes a commented config.yaml with every engine disabled. To get started, enable one driver, enable its three element sources, and install the driver's extra with `optics setup --install <name>`. See [Install Optics](https://optics-framework.org/docs/get-started/install).

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files

# Project files

> The file formats Optics reads: test cases, modules, elements, error definitions and API definitions.

An Optics project is a folder of CSV or YAML files plus a config.yaml. This page lists every file format Optics reads, the exact columns and keys, and what a run writes back.

For a guided introduction, see [Write a test](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/write) and [Write tests in YAML](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/yaml).

## How Optics finds your files

Optics walks the whole project folder, including subfolders, and decides what each `.csv`, `.yml` and `.yaml` file is by its **content**, not its name or location. You can use any folder layout. We recommend the one `optics init` creates:

```tree
birch-tests/
├── config.yaml
├── test_cases/test_cases.csv
├── modules/modules.csv
├── test_data/elements.csv
└── test_data/error_definitions.csv    # optional
```

| File type | CSV: the header row must contain | YAML: top-level key |
|---|---|---|
| Test cases | `test_case` and `test_step` | `Test Cases` |
| Modules | `module_name` and `module_step` | `Modules` |
| Elements | `Element_Name` and `Element_ID` | `Elements` |
| Error definitions | `error_code` and `match_string` | Not supported |
| API definitions | Not supported | `api` |
| Config | Not applicable | `driver_sources` and `elements_sources` |

A project needs at least one test cases file and one modules file. Elements, error definitions and API files are optional. You can split each type across several files.

CSV column names match in any case, and Optics ignores spaces around them. `element_name` works as well as `Element_Name`.

**Common mistake:**
Write YAML keys exactly as shown. Optics recognizes `test_cases:` as a test cases file, but then reads nothing from it, because the reader expects `Test Cases`.

When two files define the same thing:

- **Test cases** and **modules** with the same name: the file read last wins, with a warning in the log.
- **Elements** with the same name: the values are combined into one fallback list.

Image files (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.bmp`) anywhere in the project are available as image templates by file name. If two images share a name, one of them is used.

## Test cases

Each row adds one step to a test case. A step names a module. Rows run in order, and a test case can span rows anywhere in the file.

**CSV**

`test_cases/test_cases.csv`:

```csv
test_case,test_step
Suite Setup,Open Birch
Shopper can sign in,Sign In
Shopper can sign in,Check Home Screen
Shopper can add a shoe,Search For Trail Runner
Shopper can add a shoe,Add To Cart
Suite Teardown,Close Birch
```
**YAML**

`test_cases/test_cases.yaml`:

```yaml
Test Cases:
  - Suite Setup:
      - Open Birch
  - Shopper can sign in:
      - Sign In
      - Check Home Screen
  - Shopper can add a shoe:
      - Search For Trail Runner
      - Add To Cart
  - Suite Teardown:
      - Close Birch
```

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `test_case` | The test case name. Rows with an empty name are skipped. |
| `test_step` | The name of a module to run. Rows with an empty step are skipped. |

Within a test case, the first failing step fails the test case and skips its remaining steps. The next test case still runs.

**Warning:**
A `test_step` that names a keyword instead of a module passes both `dry_run` and `execute` but runs nothing. Put keywords in a module and name the module here.

### Setup and teardown

Optics gives a special role to a test case whose name ends with one of these words. Matching ignores case.

| Name ends with | Role | When it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `Suite Setup` | Suite setup | Once, before all other test cases. |
| `Suite Teardown` | Suite teardown | Once, after all other test cases. |
| `Setup` | Per-test setup | Before each test case. |
| `Teardown` | Per-test teardown | After each test case. |

`Web Suite Setup` is the suite setup, and `Test Setup` is the per-test setup. A name such as `Setup wizard works` does not end with one of the words, so it is an ordinary test case.

- A project has a maximum of one test case of each role. A second one stops the run before it starts, with E0503: "The test cases have more than one test setup". Rename the other test cases.
- If the suite setup fails, no other test case runs, except the suite teardown. The report shows each one as `NOT_RUN` with a `<skipped>` message that starts with `Suite setup failed:`.
- If a per-test setup fails, its test case does not run. The report shows the test case as `NOT_RUN` with a `<skipped>` message that starts with `Setup failed:`. The per-test teardown still runs.
- The test cases in the table run even when `include` or `exclude` does not name them.
- Each run of a per-test setup or teardown has its own result in the report. Its name is the name of the setup or teardown, followed by the test case, such as `Setup (Shopper can sign in)`.
- `optics execute --runner pytest` obeys the same rules.

## Modules

Each row is one keyword step. A module is the rows that share a `module_name`, in order.

**CSV**

`modules/modules.csv`:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2,param_3
Open Birch,Launch App,,,
Sign In,Assert Presence,${email_field},20,
Sign In,Enter Text,${email_field},ana@birch.example,
Sign In,Enter Text,${password_field},@:s3cret,
Sign In,Press Element,${sign_in},,
Search For Trail Runner,Press Element,${search_bar},,
Search For Trail Runner,Enter Text,${search_bar},Trail Runner 2,
Add To Cart,Press Element,${add_to_cart},index=0,
Close Birch,Close And Terminate App,,,
```
**YAML**

`modules/modules.yaml`:

```yaml
Modules:
  - Open Birch:
      - Launch App
  - Sign In:
      - Assert Presence ${email_field} 20
      - Enter Text ${email_field} ana@birch.example
      - Enter Text ${password_field} @:s3cret
      - Press Element ${sign_in}
  - Search For Trail Runner:
      - Press Element ${search_bar}
      - Enter Text ${search_bar} "Trail Runner 2"
  - Add To Cart:
      - Press Element ${add_to_cart} index=0
  - Close Birch:
      - Close And Terminate App
```

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `module_name` | The module name. |
| `module_step` | A keyword name, such as `Press Element`. Case and spaces don't matter: `press_element` works too. To run another module from inside a module, use `Execute Module,<name>`. |
| `param_1`, `param_2`, … | The keyword's parameters, in order. Add as many `param_` columns as you need. |

Parameter rules:

- **Empty cells are dropped**, and the values after them move left. You can't skip a parameter by leaving its cell blank. Use a named parameter instead.
- **Named parameters** are written `name=value`, for example `index=0` or `timeout_str=20`. They work only when `name` is a real parameter of that keyword. Anything else, such as `text=Sign in` or `css=#search`, stays a positional value.
- **Variables** written as a whole cell, `${email_field}`, are replaced with the element's values. A variable inside a longer value, as in `Hello ${name}!` or `${first} ${last}`, is replaced with its first value. An unknown name fails the step with [E0403](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e04-keywords-and-parameters). Write `$${name}` to type a literal `${name}`.
- **Locators first.** If a keyword's first parameter is `element`, a first value that starts with `text=`, `css=` or `xpath=` is the element. `Enter Text,text=Name,Ava` types `Ava` into the element `text=Name`.
- **store_as.** Add `store_as=<name>` to a step to save the keyword's result as `${name}` for later steps and test cases. Lists and dictionaries are saved as JSON. See [Store a result](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/#store-as).
- Values starting with `/`, `//` or `(` are always positional, so XPaths are never mistaken for named parameters.

In YAML, a step is one string. The keyword name is matched first, and the rest is split on spaces. Wrap a value with spaces in quotes: `"Trail Runner 2"`. Wrap multi-word module names you pass as parameters in quotes too: `Run Loop "Add To Cart" 3`.

See [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/) for each keyword's parameters.

## Elements

Each row gives a name to a locator or a value. Steps refer to it as `${name}`.

**CSV**

`test_data/elements.csv`:

```csv
Element_Name,Element_ID,Element_ID_text,Element_ID_image
email_field,//android.widget.EditText[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/email'],Email,
password_field,//android.widget.EditText[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/password'],Password,
sign_in,//android.widget.Button[@text='Sign in'],Sign in,sign_in.png
search_bar,//*[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/search'],Search,
add_to_cart,text=Add to cart,,add_to_cart.png
```
**YAML**

`test_data/elements.yaml`:

```yaml
Elements:
  email_field:
    - //android.widget.EditText[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/email']
    - Email
  sign_in: ["//android.widget.Button[@text='Sign in']", "Sign in", "sign_in.png"]
  search_bar: "//*[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/search']"
  add_to_cart: ["text=Add to cart", "add_to_cart.png"]
```

| Column | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `Element_Name` | The name. |
| `Element_ID` | The first locator or value. Required. |
| `Element_ID_*` | Fallbacks. Any column whose header starts with `Element_ID`, such as `Element_ID_text`, `Element_ID_image` or `Element_ID_2`, adds another value. They're tried in column order. |

- Empty cells are ignored. Columns that don't start with `Element_ID`, such as `Element_Text`, are ignored.
- A second row with the same name adds more fallback values.
- When a step uses `${name}`, Optics tries each value in turn until the step passes, up to 20 attempts. It moves on only when the element isn't found. Steps inside `Run Loop`, `Condition` and `Execute Module` use only the first value.
- Variables that a step creates while running, such as the target of `Evaluate`, `Read Data` or `store_as`, need no row. Do not add a placeholder row for them.

Optics decides what kind of locator a value is from its form:

| Value | Treated as |
|---|---|
| Starts with `text=` or `text_only:` | Text. `text_only:` uses OCR only. |
| Ends with `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.bmp` | An image template, found by file name anywhere in the project. |
| Starts with `css=` | CSS selector. |
| Starts with `xpath=`, `/`, `//` or `(` | XPath. |
| Starts with `android.` or `xcui` | A UI class name. |
| Starts with `.` or `#`, or contains `[` and `]` | CSS selector. |
| Anything else | Text. |

Text like `(optional)` or `Size [US]` is read as XPath or CSS. Add `text=` in front to force text: `text=Size [US]`. See [Define elements](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/define).

## Error definitions

A CSV file of messages that mean your app is in a bad state. In `optics execute`, Optics checks the text on the final screen against each `match_string`. It reads the screen before Suite Teardown when the suite has one.

`test_data/error_definitions.csv`:

```csv
error_code,match_string,description,severity
BIRCH_001,Unfortunately,App crashed with a system dialog,critical
BIRCH_002,Something went wrong,Birch showed its generic error screen,high
BIRCH_003,Out of stock,Product page shows out of stock,medium
```

| Column | Required | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `error_code` | Yes | Your code for this error. A repeated code replaces the earlier row. |
| `match_string` | Yes | Text to look for. Matching ignores case and finds the text anywhere in the screen's text. It isn't a regular expression. |
| `description` | No | Free text, shown in the results. |
| `severity` | No | Free text, for example `critical`, `high` or `medium`. |

There is no YAML form. A match adds a failing test case to `junit_output.xml` and gives exit code `1`. See [Catch error screens](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/error-detection).

## API definitions

A YAML file with a top-level `api:` key defines HTTP calls that the `Invoke API` keyword makes. You can also put the `api:` block inside config.yaml.

`test_data/api.yaml`:

```yaml
api:
  collections:
    birch:                                  # collection id, used in Invoke API
      name: Birch API
      base_url: https://api.birch.example
      global_headers:
        Accept: application/json
      apis:
        get_product:                        # API id
          name: Get product
          description: Look up Trail Runner 2
          endpoint: /v1/products/trail-runner-2
          request:
            method: GET
            headers: {}
            body: null
          expected_result:
            jsonpath_assertions:
              - path: $.name
                condition: "$ == 'Trail Runner 2'"
            extract:
              product_price: $.price        # saves ${product_price}
```

Call it from a module with `Invoke API,birch.get_product`. Only the top-level key `api` works; a file whose top key is `apis` is recognized but loads nothing. See [Call an API](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/api-calls).

## Escaping and special values

**CSV quoting.** Wrap a cell in double quotes when it contains a comma, and double any quotes inside it:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1
Find Shoe,Press Element,"//*[contains(@text,'Trail Runner 2')]"
Go Home,Execute Script,"{""script"": ""mobile: pressKey"", ""args"": {""keycode"": 3}}"
```

**Backslash sequences.** In any cell, `\n` becomes a new line, `\t` a tab, `\r` a carriage return, and `\\` a single backslash.

**Secrets.** Start a value with `@:`, as in `@:s3cret`, to mask it as `****` in the console, the log files, `logs.json`, `junit_output.xml`, the result tree and error output. Every driver removes the prefix before typing. Optics also masks these items: values saved under secret names, passwords in URLs, and secret values from config.yaml. See [Hide sensitive values](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/variables#hide-sensitive-values).

**Encoding.** Save files as UTF-8. Some spreadsheet apps add a byte order mark (BOM) at the start of the file, which can stop Optics recognizing the header row.

**YAML quoting.** Optics removes the quotes around a value, also when the value contains `=`: `Condition "${size} == '9'" "Pick Size" "Show Error"`.

## Outputs

`optics execute` and `optics dry_run` write to `execution_output/` in the project, unless you set `execution_output_path` in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config).

```tree
birch-tests/execution_output/
├── junit_output.xml
├── logs.json                                      # json_log: true
├── internal_logs.log                              # file_log: true
├── execution_logs.log                             # file_log: true
├── 2026-10-09T15-04-05-123456-pre_press_element.jpg
├── ...-press_element_element_detection_result.jpg
├── ...-failure_<test case>.jpg                    # when a test case fails
├── ...-failure_<test case>.xml                    # when a test case fails
├── ...-end_of_run.jpg
├── page_sources_log.xml
├── failed_steps_elements.json                     # when a step fails
└── detected_errors_<session_id>.json              # only when error definitions match
```

| File | When it's written | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `junit_output.xml` | Every run that starts, including dry runs. It is also written when you stop the run with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. | One test case per test, with each module and keyword, their status (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `ERROR` or `NOT_RUN`), start and end times, and log lines. The suite and every `classname` are named after the project folder. Error detection adds a failing `on-screen-error-detection` test case. If another session in the same process is already writing the file, Optics names it `junit_output_<session_id>.xml`. See [Read the results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results#read-the-junit-report). |
| `logs.json` | `json_log: true` | A JSON list of every test case, module and keyword event with status and timings. |
| `internal_logs.log`, `execution_logs.log` | `file_log: true` | Text logs. Each rotates at 10 MB. |
| `<time>-pre_<keyword>.jpg` | Every keyword that finds an element, with `save_captures: true` | The screen before Optics looked for the element. |
| `<time>-<keyword>_element_detection_result.jpg` | An element was found in the UI tree, with `save_captures: true` | The screen with a green box around the element. |
| `<time>-<keyword>_image_detection_result.jpg` | An element was found by OCR or image, with `save_captures: true` | The screen with a green box, and a red dot at the tap point for text. |
| `<time>-<keyword>_with_aoi.jpg` | The step used an area of interest, with `save_captures: true` | The screen with the area drawn in blue. |
| `<time>-<keyword>.jpg` | Gestures and coordinate keywords, such as `Swipe`, `Scroll`, `Press By Percentage`, `Press Keycode` | The screen when the step ran. |
| `<time>-capture_screenshot.jpg` | `Capture Screenshot`, `Get Screen Elements` | Only when `save_captures` is `true`. |
| `<time>-failure_<test case>.jpg` and `.xml` | A test case failed, with `save_captures: true`. Web pages write `.html`. | The screen and the UI tree where the test case ended. |
| `<time>-end_of_run.jpg` | End of `optics execute`, before Suite Teardown, if the app is still open | The final screen. |
| `page_sources_log.xml` | Appium page source reads and the end of the run | Each UI tree, with a timestamp. |
| `page_sources_log.html` | Web page source reads and the end of the run | Each page's HTML, with a timestamp. |
| `failed_steps_elements.json` | A step failed, with `save_captures: true` | For each failed step: the test case, the step and the elements on the screen, with secrets masked. Use it to fix the locator. |
| `interactable_elements.json` | `Get Interactive Elements`, `Get Screen Elements` | The latest list of elements on screen. |
| `api_details.log`, `api_details.har` | `Invoke API` | Each request and response. |
| `detected_errors_<session_id>.json` | Error definitions matched at the end of the run | The codes, matched text, descriptions and severities. |

Screenshots are JPEG files named `<timestamp>-<name>.jpg`.

`optics live` writes elsewhere: `screenshots/session_<time>/` and `logs/optics_live_<time>.log` in the project. See [Read results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results).

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines

# Engines and extras

> Learn which drivers, element sources, OCR, image matching and LLM engines Optics supports, and which pip extra installs each one.

Optics keeps its core install small. Each driver and recognition engine is a separate pip extra that you add for your platform, either with [`optics setup`](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#optics-setup) or with pip. You then turn the engine on by name in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#engine-lists).

The name you write in config.yaml is the engine's name in the tables below. The extra is what you install.

## Drivers

A driver controls the device or browser. Enable one under `driver_sources`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appium` | `appium` | Native and hybrid apps through an Appium server. | Android, iOS, Android TV, Samsung Tizen TV, LG webOS TV |
| `selenium` | `selenium` | Websites through a Selenium server or Grid. Chrome and Firefox only. | Web |
| `playwright` | `playwright` | Websites in Chromium, Firefox or WebKit, with no server to run. It can also connect to a remote browser, emulate a phone, and start signed in with a Chrome or Edge profile. | Web |
| `ble` | `ble` | Taps and typing through a Bluetooth mouse-and-keyboard dongle, for devices with no automation access. | Any device that accepts a Bluetooth mouse and keyboard |

The Appium server itself, and its UiAutomator2 or XCUITest driver, aren't Python packages. Install and start them separately. See [Test Android apps](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/android) and [Test iOS apps](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/ios).

## Element sources

An element source is how Optics looks at the screen for a driver. They need no extra of their own: they come with their driver. Enable them under `elements_sources`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appium_find_element` | `appium` | Finds elements by XPath, accessibility id or class. | Android, iOS, TV |
| `appium_page_source` | `appium` | Searches the UI tree by XPath and text. Lists interactive elements. | Android, iOS, TV |
| `appium_screenshot` | `appium` | Screenshots for OCR, image matching and AI self-heal. | Android, iOS, TV |
| `appium_web` | `appium` | Finds `css=` and DOM XPath locators in web pages in the phone's browser and in WebViews. Lists interactive elements. | Android, iOS |
| `selenium_find_element` | `selenium` | Finds elements by XPath, text, id, name, CSS or link text. | Web |
| `selenium_page_source` | `selenium` | Searches the page HTML. | Web |
| `selenium_screenshot` | `selenium` | Screenshots for OCR and image matching. | Web |
| `playwright_find_element` | `playwright` | Finds elements by `xpath=`, `css=`, `text=`, `label=`, `alt=`, `title=`, `role=`, `id=`, `testid=` and other locators. | Web |
| `playwright_page_source` | `playwright` | Searches the page and lists interactive elements. | Web |
| `playwright_screenshot` | `playwright` | Screenshots for OCR and image matching. | Web |
| `camera_screenshot` | None | Frames from a webcam, an HTTP(S) screenshot URL (with an optional bearer token) or a TCP frame server. | Any, usually with `ble` |

Only `appium_page_source`, `appium_web` and `playwright_page_source` can list interactive elements. With Selenium, `Get Interactive Elements`, the HTTP `/elements` endpoint and the MCP elements resource fail with [E0202](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e02-elements).

## Text recognition (OCR)

OCR finds elements by the text visible in a screenshot. Optics uses it when the UI tree doesn't have the text, or when you write `text_only:`. Enable engines under `text_detection`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `easyocr` | `easyocr` | Local OCR. Accurate but slow on CPU. Downloads its models the first time it runs. English only. | All |
| `pytesseract` | `pytesseract` | Local OCR with Tesseract. Needs the Tesseract program installed and on your PATH. Matches whole words. | All |
| `google_vision` | `google-vision` | Google Cloud Vision. Needs a Vision API key in `api_key`, a service account key file in `credentials_path`, or `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. Set only one of `api_key` and `credentials_path`. | All |
| `remote_ocr` | None | Your own OCR service over HTTP. Set its `url`. | All |

We recommend `easyocr` to start with. It needs nothing else installed.

## Image matching

Image matching finds an element by a template image you saved in the project. Enable engines under `image_detection`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `templatematch` | None | Local matching. Finds templates even when they're scaled or rotated. | All |
| `remote_oir` | None | Your own image matching service over HTTP. Set its `url`. | All |

## LLM

An LLM powers [AI self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal) and the plain-English mode of `optics live`. Enable one under `llm_models`.

| Name in config | Extra | What it's for | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gemini` | `gemini` | Google Gemini, through the Gemini API or Vertex AI. Set `credentials_path` to a service account key file to use Vertex AI. Default model `gemini-2.5-flash`. | All |
| `openai` | `openai` | OpenAI, and any server with an OpenAI-compatible API: OpenRouter, Azure OpenAI, or a local model in Ollama, vLLM or LM Studio. | All |
| `anthropic` | `anthropic` | Claude, through the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI. | All |

Each engine reads its API key from `capabilities.api_key` in config.yaml, else from the environment. See [llm_models](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#llm-models) for its settings and credentials.

## Other extras

| Extra | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `mcp` | The [MCP server](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp), `optics mcp`. Install it with pip; `optics setup` can't install it, and the `all` bundle doesn't include it. |

## Bundles

A bundle installs several extras at once.

| Bundle | Installs |
|---|---|
| `mobile` | `appium` |
| `web` | `selenium`, `playwright` |
| `vision` | `easyocr`, `pytesseract`, `google-vision` |
| `llm` | `gemini`, `openai`, `anthropic` |
| `all` | `appium`, `ble`, `selenium`, `playwright`, `easyocr`, `pytesseract`, `google-vision`, `gemini`, `openai`, `anthropic`. Not `mcp`. |

## Install with optics setup

`optics setup` installs extras into the same Python environment Optics runs in.

```text
optics setup [--install NAME [NAME ...]] [--list]
```

Without flags, it opens a picker with a checkbox for each engine. In scripts and CI, name the engines:

```shell
$ optics setup --install appium easyocr
$ optics setup --install web gemini
$ optics setup --install appium==6.1.2
```

- Names are case-insensitive. Use an extra name, a display name such as `Gemini` or `Google Vision`, or a bundle.
- Pin the engine's main package with a version specifier: `appium==6.1.2`, `"easyocr>=1.7,<2.0"`. The version must be in the range that your Optics release supports. Use an operator such as `==`; `appium=6.1.2` is an error. Bundles can't take a version.
- Optics keeps itself at the version you have, so installing an engine never upgrades Optics.
- Installing `playwright` also downloads the Chromium browser. A [remote browser](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#use-a-remote-browser) needs no download.

`optics setup --list` prints every name:

```terminal
Available engines (install with `optics setup --install <name>`):

Action Drivers:
  appium          (appium-python-client)
  ble             (pyserial)
  selenium        (selenium)
  playwright      (playwright)

OCR Engines:
  easyocr         (easyocr)
  pytesseract     (pytesseract, pillow)
  google-vision   (google-cloud-vision)

LLM Engines:
  gemini          (google-genai)
  openai          (openai)
```
