```terminal
  anthropic       (anthropic)

Bundles (install several at once):
  mobile          (appium)
  web             (selenium, playwright)
  vision          (easyocr, pytesseract, google-vision)
  llm             (gemini, openai, anthropic)
  all             (appium, ble, selenium, playwright, easyocr, pytesseract, google-vision, gemini, openai, anthropic)
```

On success, Optics reminds you that services such as the Appium server still need to be started separately. Run `optics doctor` to confirm each engine shows ✅.

## Install with pip

Name the extras in brackets:

```shell
$ pip install "optics-framework[appium,easyocr]"
$ pip install "optics-framework[playwright]" && playwright install chromium
$ pip install "optics-framework[mcp]"
```

If you installed Optics with the [install script](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#install-scripts), pass extras with `--extra appium,easyocr` (or `OPTICS_EXTRA` on Windows).

## Where installs are refused

`optics setup` and `optics quickstart` refuse to install into environments that another tool manages, because changing them would break that tool. `optics doctor` shows an `environment` ⚠️ row when this applies.

| Environment | What to do instead |
|---|---|
| Conda | Use a virtual environment. EasyOCR and Optics need conflicting versions of NumPy under Conda. |
| `pipx` | Reinstall with the extras: `pipx install --force "optics-framework[appium,easyocr]"`, or add packages with `pipx inject optics-framework <package>`. |
| `uv tool` or `uvx` | Reinstall with the extras: `uv tool install "optics-framework[appium,easyocr]"`. |
| A project managed by uv, Poetry, PDM or Pipenv | Add the extra with your tool, for example `uv add "optics-framework[appium]"` or `poetry add "optics-framework[appium]"`. |
| System Python marked as externally managed | Use a virtual environment. |
| Read-only site-packages | Use a virtual environment you can write to. |
| No pip and no uv | Install pip, or use a virtual environment. |

To create a virtual environment:

**macOS and Linux**

```shell
$ python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install optics-framework
```
**Windows**

```powershell
PS> python -m venv .venv; .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1; pip install optics-framework
```

In a virtual environment without pip, `optics setup` uses `uv` if it's available.

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp

# MCP server reference

> Tools and resources that `optics mcp` gives your AI agent.

`optics mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, a standard way for AI agents such as Claude, Cursor or VS Code to call outside tools. Your agent starts a session on a device or browser, reads the screen as a list of rows, and acts on those rows by reference. Each action returns what changed on the screen.

For a guided walkthrough, see [Build tests with an AI agent](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/agent).

## Install

The server needs the `mcp` extra. The [install scripts](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#install-scripts) always include it. With pip, add it yourself: `optics setup` can't install it, and the `all` bundle doesn't include it.

```shell
$ pip install "optics-framework[mcp]"
```

The extra installs fastmcp 3.4.4 or newer.

You also need the extras for your driver, for example `appium` or `playwright`. See [Engines and extras](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines).

## Start the server

```text
optics mcp [--transport stdio|http] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--toolset core|full]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--transport` | `stdio` | `stdio`: your agent starts the server and talks to it directly. `http`: the server listens at `http://<host>:<port>/mcp`. |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. `http` only. |
| `--port` | `8090` | The port to listen on. `http` only. |
| `--toolset` | `OPTICS_MCP_TOOLSET`, else `core` | `core`: the 10 tools below. `full`: also one tool for each keyword. See [Full toolset](#full-toolset). |

We recommend `stdio` for an agent on your own machine. Use `http` when the server runs in a container or on another machine.

Over `http`, each session belongs to the client connection that started it. Another client cannot see the session or use its id. The server has no authentication, so keep it on `127.0.0.1` or behind a gateway that adds authentication. On another address, it logs a warning when it starts. Set `OPTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` to the host names that clients use, such as `localhost` in a container. A request with another `Host` is refused.

An `http` server also refuses what makes it read its own files: `project_path`, `credentials_path`, `file:` URLs and `Read Data` from a file.

## Connect your agent

Most agents read a JSON file that lists MCP servers. For Claude Desktop it's `claude_desktop_config.json`; for Claude Code it's `.mcp.json` in your project. Other agents use the same shape.

`.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "optics": {
      "command": "optics",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

If your agent can't find `optics`, use the full path to it, for example `/Users/ana/.optics/bin/optics`.

For the `http` transport, point the agent at the URL instead:

`.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "optics": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

When the server runs in Docker and Appium runs on your machine, pass `url: "http://host.docker.internal:4723"` to `start_session`.

## Screen rows

The server shows the screen as rows. Each row has a ref, such as `e7`, that the agent uses as a target:

```text
e2 input "Username" [tap,input] #user-name
e4 input "Login" [tap] #login-button
e6 h4 "Accepted usernames are:"
```

- The quoted text is on the screen. The `#id` is not.
- `[...]` lists what the element accepts: `tap`, `long`, `toggle`, `input` or `scroll`. A row without it is read-only text.
- A web row marked `(off-screen)` is on the page but scrolled out of view. A tap scrolls it into view.
- A ref stays valid while its element is on the screen. A ref from an earlier screen gives a `stale_ref` error.

A tap on a ref uses a locator that matches only that element. The agent can also pass an exact label or a locator (`css=`, `xpath=`, `text=`) as the target.

## Core tools

The default toolset has 10 tools. Every tool except `start_session` takes `session_id`. You can leave it out when one session is open. When more than one session is open, the call fails with `session_required` and lists the ids.

| Tool | Parameters (defaults) | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `start_session` | See [start_session](#start-session) | Starts a session. With `app`, it also opens the app or URL and returns the first screen. |
| `terminate_session` | none | Ends the session and closes the driver. |
| `observe` | `query` (""), `screenshot` (false), `max_rows` (80, 1–300) | Lists the rows. `query` keeps rows whose label or id holds the text. `screenshot` adds a JPEG of at most 1024 px. |
| `tap` | `target`, `repeat` (1, 1–20) | Runs `press_element`. Refuses a row that has no `tap`, `long`, `toggle` or `input`. |
| `type_text` | `target`, `text`, `clear_first` (false) | Runs `enter_text`, after `clear_element_text` when `clear_first` is true. Refuses a row without `input`. |
| `scroll` | `direction` (`up`, `down`, `left`, `right`), `until` (""), `timeout_s` (10, 1–60) | Runs `scroll`. With `until`, runs `scroll_until_element_appears` (up and down only). |
| `press_key` | `key` | `back` runs `go_back` on any driver. Another value runs `press_keycode`: a key name such as `Enter`, `Escape`, `esc` or `ArrowDown`, or an Android KeyEvent number such as `66`. On the web, case and a `KEYCODE_` prefix do not matter. A ref is refused with a hint to use `tap`. |
| `launch_app` | `app` ("") | Opens an app id or a URL. Empty opens the configured app. |
| `check` | `present` ([]), `absent` ([]), `timeout_s` (5, 0–30) | Waits for the texts or refs, then gives a verdict. See [check](#check). |
| `run_keyword` | `keyword`, `params` ({}) | Runs any other keyword. See [run_keyword](#run-keyword). |

The tools that act (`tap`, `type_text`, `scroll`, `press_key`, `launch_app` and `run_keyword`) also take these parameters:

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `expect_present` | `[]` | Texts or refs that must be on the screen after the action. |
| `expect_absent` | `[]` | Texts or refs that must be gone after the action. |
| `screen` | `diff` | What the reply shows: `diff` (the changed rows), `full` (all rows) or `none`. |

### start_session

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `driver` | `appium` | `appium`, `selenium`, `playwright` or `ble`. |
| `app` | "" | An app id or URL to open after the session starts. |
| `url` | Appium: `http://127.0.0.1:4723` | The driver's server URL. For Playwright, the endpoint of a [remote browser](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#use-a-remote-browser). |
| `capabilities` | `{}` | The driver's capabilities, as in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#examples-by-platform). For a phone-sized page, add `"device": "Pixel 7"`. See [Emulate a phone](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#emulate-a-phone). For a signed-in web session, add `profile`. See [Sign in with a browser profile](#sign-in-with-a-browser-profile). |
| `elements_sources` | Every source of the driver | For Appium: `appium_find_element`, `appium_page_source`, `appium_web` and `appium_screenshot`. Passing `[]` makes the session fail to start. |
| `text_detection` | `[]` | OCR engines, for example `["easyocr"]`. |
| `image_detection` | `[]` | Image engines, for example `["templatematch"]`. |
| `project_path` | "" | A project folder. Optics loads its image templates. It doesn't load elements or test cases. `stdio` only: an `http` server refuses it with E0501. |
| `ai_self_heal` | `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL`, else off | Turns on [AI self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal). |
| `llm_provider` | `OPTICS_LLM_PROVIDER`, else `gemini` | The LLM engine for self-heal: `gemini`, `openai` or `anthropic`. |
| `llm_model` | `OPTICS_LLM_MODEL`, else `gemini-2.5-flash` for Gemini | The model for self-heal. `openai` and `anthropic` need one. |
| `strict_element_match` | false | Accepts only exact text matches. |

It returns `{"session_id", "driver", "idle_lease_s", "status": "started", "driver_id"}`. With `app`, it also returns the first screen:

```text
session e5202adb-44cd-43c6-b84a-c31186dd67b7 (playwright) · idle lease 900 s
launch_app "https://www.saucedemo.com" -> ok · verified: unknown (add expect_present/expect_absent to verify)
screen 0b1dab · 8 rows
e1 div "Swag Labs"
e2 input "Username" [tap,input] #user-name
e3 input "Password" [tap,input] #password
e4 input "Login" [tap] #login-button
...
```

The server refuses a `${NAME}` reference in `url` or in a `capabilities.headers` value, because it does not read its own environment for a caller. It also refuses `capabilities.storage_state` as a file path. Send the state as a JSON object. Both give `E0501`.

The first session against a remote device farm can take 30 to 60 seconds to start.

### Sign in with a browser profile

A web flow that needs a sign-in can start with the sign-ins of a local Chrome or Edge profile. The agent reads the `optics://browser-profiles` resource and shows the list to you. Each entry has a `channel`, a `directory`, a `name` and the `email` of the account:

```json
[{"channel": "chrome", "directory": "Default", "name": "Work", "email": "me@example.com"}]
```

After you choose a profile, the agent passes its `directory`, `name` or `email` as `capabilities.profile`:

```json
{
  "driver": "playwright",
  "capabilities": {"profile": "me@example.com"},
  "app": "https://app.example.com"
}
```

The browser starts with the sign-ins of that profile. If you choose no profile, the agent asks you for the credentials and types them with `type_text`. A `profile` that matches none, or more than one, fails with `E0501` and lists the profiles. Add `channel` (`chrome`, `chrome-beta` or `msedge`) to choose between browsers.

A profile holds the sign-ins of the person who runs the server. For this reason only a `stdio` server lists and accepts profiles. The `http` transport and `optics serve` refuse `profile`. Every API session refuses `user_data_dir`. Set both in the `config.yaml` of a project instead. See [Start signed in with a browser profile](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#start-signed-in-with-a-browser-profile) for what a profile carries over.

### Action replies

Each tool that acts replies with one head line, the check lines, then the screen:

```text
tap e4 "Login" -> ok (Text) · verified: pass
check present "Products": met
screen 65a355 · new screen
e9 button "Open Menu" [tap] #react-burger-menu-btn
e12 a "Cart, empty" [tap]
e13 span "Products"
...
```

- `ok` means only that the keyword ran. The word in brackets is the strategy that found the element.
- `verified` is `pass`, `fail` or `unknown`. It is `pass` only when every expectation is met and the action caused it. Without `expect_present` or `expect_absent`, it stays `unknown`.
- An action waits up to 5 seconds for `expect_present` and `expect_absent` before it judges them. A page that loads after a redirect can still pass.
- `note:` lines tell the agent what to trust less. For example, a `scroll` is `ok` even when nothing moved, and a row with no unique locator is found by its label.
- `run_keyword` adds a `result:` line with the keyword's return value, cut at 400 characters.

After an action, the server reads the screen until it stops changing. A screen with no rows counts as a page that is still loading, so the server reads it again for up to 6 seconds. A keyword that only reads, and `execute_script` when the screen stays the same, are read once.

The structured reply is `{"ok", "verified", "verb", "keyword", "checks", "target", "result", "screen", "error"}`. `screen` holds `digest`, `changed`, `new_screen`, `added`, `removed` and `relabelled`. On a new screen, `screen` holds all `rows` and no `added` or `removed` lists. With `screen="none"`, `screen` holds only `digest`, `changed` and `new_screen`. The reply text is cut at 8,000 characters.

When self-heal recovers a step, `result` is `{"result", "healed": true, "heal_summary", "suggested_steps"}`, so your agent can write the extra steps into the test.

### check

`check` reads the screen until every text in `present` shows and every text in `absent` is gone, or until `timeout_s` passes. It gives a verdict, not an error:

```text
check -> passed
present "Products": met
absent "Login": met
```

A locator in `present`, such as `css=.title`, gets one look with `assert_presence`. `absent` cannot hold a locator. The structured reply is `{"passed", "checks", "digest"}`.

### run_keyword

`run_keyword` runs a keyword that has no tool of its own, for example `assert_text`, `select_dropdown_option` or `get_text`. `params` takes the keyword's parameters by name, as strings. An element parameter can be a ref:

```json
{"keyword": "get_text", "params": {"element": "css=.title"}}
```

```text
run_keyword get_text -> ok (Text) · verified: unknown (add expect_present/expect_absent to verify)
result: Products
screen 65a355 · unchanged
```

The `optics://keywords` resource lists every keyword that `run_keyword` accepts. Flow control, deprecated keywords and the coordinate keywords are not in it. Optics caps a `timeout` parameter at 60 seconds.

## Full toolset

Start the server with `--toolset full`, or set `OPTICS_MCP_TOOLSET=full`, to add one tool for each app, action and verification keyword. The tool name is the keyword in snake_case, such as `press_element`, `enter_text`, `assert_text` or `go_back`. Each tool takes `session_id` plus the keyword's parameters, all as strings. An element parameter can be a ref. See [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/) for each parameter.

The full toolset also has:

- The 10 core tools, but the keyword tools `launch_app` and `scroll` replace the core tools of the same name.
- `screenshot`, which returns the screen as a PNG image.
- Deprecated keywords, `swipe`, `get_interactive_elements`, `initialise_setup`, `start_appium_session` and `get_driver_session_id`.

A keyword tool returns the keyword's result, and an error raises with `[E0201] message`. It does not return the screen.

## Coordinate taps

Agents that guess coordinates write fragile tests, so the server hides the coordinate keywords by default. Set `OPTICS_MCP_ALLOW_COORDINATE_TAPS=1` before you start the server to allow them:

- In the core toolset, `run_keyword` and `optics://keywords` then accept `press_by_coordinates`, `press_by_percentage` and `swipe`.
- In the full toolset, the `press_by_coordinates` and `press_by_percentage` tools appear.

Self-heal can still tap by percentage when it recovers a step.

## Resources

Resources are read-only data your agent can fetch by URI.

| URI | Type | What it returns |
|---|---|---|
| `optics://keywords` | JSON | The keywords `run_keyword` accepts, with the description, parameters, `returns` and `deprecated` of each. |
| `optics://project-format` | Markdown | How to write a CSV project: the files, columns, `${name}` variables, secrets and flow-control keywords. |
| `optics://browser-profiles` | JSON | The Chrome and Edge profiles on the machine that runs the server, as `{channel, directory, name, email}`. Use one as `capabilities.profile`. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/screenshot` | PNG | The current screen. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/source` | JSON | `{"page_source", "timestamp"}`: the UI tree or HTML. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/elements` | JSON | The elements on the screen as `{i, label, cls, bounds, act, rid, loc, offscreen}`. Appium, Appium web and Playwright only. It has no refs. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/screen_elements` | JSON | `{"screenshot", "elements"}`: a base64 PNG and the elements in the same frame. |
| `optics://session/{session_id}/steps` | JSON | The steps the session ran, with the module and element CSV rows to replay them. |

There are no MCP prompts.

### The steps resource

`/steps` returns `{"steps", "modules_csv", "elements_csv", "notes"}`. Each step that passed is a row in the module `recorded`, and each element it used is a row in the elements CSV. A value typed into a secret field becomes its own element, written as `<redacted>`:

`modules_csv`:

```csv
module_name,module_step,param_1,param_2
recorded,Launch App,https://www.saucedemo.com
recorded,Enter Text,${username_input},standard_user
recorded,Enter Text,${password_input},${password_value}
recorded,Press Element,${login_input}
```

`elements_csv`:

```csv
Element_Name,Element_ID,Element_ID_2,Element_ID_3
username_input,"css=[data-test=""username""]",css=#user-name,Username
password_input,"css=[data-test=""password""]",css=#password
password_value,<redacted>
login_input,"css=[data-test=""login-button""]",css=#login-button,Login
```

`notes` says what to do before the suite can run, for example: `replace <redacted> for password_value before running: write it as @:value or set it with Read Data,${password_value},ENV:NAME`. A passed `check` is recorded as `Assert Presence`. See [Hide sensitive values](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/variables#hide-sensitive-values).

## Environment variables

Set these in the environment that starts `optics mcp`. In a JSON client config, add an `env` object next to `command`.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OPTICS_MCP_TOOLSET` | `core` | `core` or `full`. The `--toolset` flag wins. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_SESSION_IDLE_S` | `900` | Ends a session after this many seconds without a call. `0` turns it off. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT_S` | `100` | The longest time one call can take. After it, the call returns a `timeout` error, and the session stays `busy` until the driver call ends. |
| `OPTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | | `http` only. Host names that the server answers in addition to loopback names, separated by commas. |
| `OPTICS_MCP_ALLOW_COORDINATE_TAPS` | off | `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` allows the coordinate keywords. See [Coordinate taps](#coordinate-taps). |
| `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL` | off | `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on` turns self-heal on for every session unless `start_session` says otherwise. |
| `OPTICS_LLM_PROVIDER` | `gemini` | The default LLM engine: `gemini`, `openai` or `anthropic`. |
| `OPTICS_LLM_MODEL` | | The default model. `openai` and `anthropic` need one. |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | | The engine's key. Keys never travel in a tool call. A session cannot set `api_key_env`, so each engine reads its default variables. For Gemini on Vertex AI, see [llm_models](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#llm-models). Claude runs only on the Claude API here, not on Bedrock or Vertex AI. |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | | The server the `openai` engine calls, such as OpenRouter or a local Ollama. Only the operator sets it; a session cannot. The key comes from `OPENAI_API_KEY`. |

## Typical agent loop

### Start a session
Call `start_session` with the driver and the app, for example `driver: "playwright"`, `app: "https://www.saucedemo.com"`. For a phone, add `url` and `capabilities`, such as `{"platformName": "Android", "appPackage": "com.birch.shop", ...}`. The reply shows the first screen.

### Act on refs
Call `tap`, `type_text` and the other tools with a ref from the rows, for example `tap(target="e4", expect_present=["Products"])`. Each reply shows what changed, so you do not need to call `observe` after each action. Use `observe` for a `query`, a screenshot or the full list.

### Check the result
Call `check` with the texts that prove the flow worked.

### Save the run as a test
Read `optics://session/{session_id}/steps` and `optics://project-format`. Write the CSV files and a config.yaml, replace each `<redacted>` value, then run `optics execute <folder>`.

### End the session
Call `terminate_session`.

## Limits

- **No flow control.** `Run Loop`, `Condition`, `Evaluate`, `Read Data`, `Invoke API` and the other flow-control keywords are not tools. Your agent can still write them into CSV modules for `optics execute`.
- **No save tool.** There are no tools to record, save, replay, find devices or run doctor. The agent writes project files from the steps resource.
- **Sessions are not shared.** Sessions live in the server's memory. `optics serve` and `optics live` cannot see them. A session ends after the idle lease. All sessions end when the server stops.
- **Images come from a project.** There is no upload tool. On `stdio`, pass `project_path` to use template images. An `http` server has no template images.
- **Selenium has no rows.** The tools run keywords on Selenium, but `verified` stays `unknown` and `observe` fails. Read `/source` instead.

## Errors

A core tool does not raise. A failed call returns an error result with the code, a `Next:` line, and the current rows:

```text
tap "Nonexistent thing" -> FAIL · verified: fail
[E0201] not found: tried Nonexistent thing.
Next: Pick a ref from the current screen.
screen 65a355 · 40 rows
e9 button "Open Menu" [tap] #react-burger-menu-btn
...
```

The structured reply has `error: {"code", "kind", "message"}`. An error without a code, such as a bad ref, has no `[E…]` part. See [Error codes](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors).

| Kind | When |
|---|---|
| `not_found` | No strategy found the element. |
| `stale_ref` | The ref is not on the current screen. |
| `unknown_ref` | No row has that ref. |
| `ambiguous` | The target matches more than one row. |
| `no_locator` | The row has no locator that matches only it. |
| `invalid_params` | A parameter is missing or wrong, such as `type_text` on a row without `input`. The reply shows an example call. |
| `silent_failure` | The keyword reported an error but did not fail (`E0401` or `E0405`). The message reads `[E0401] <keyword> reported an error: ...`. Read the screen before you continue. |
| `unsupported` | The platform does not support the keyword. |
| `loop` | The same action ran 3 times in a row without progress. The fourth try does not run. |
| `timeout` | The call took longer than `OPTICS_MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT_S`. |
| `busy` | An earlier call on the session still runs. |
| `session_lost` | The driver session ended. Start a new session. |
| `unknown_session` | No such session, or none is open. When the idle lease ended it, the message says so. |
| `session_required` | More than one session is open, and `session_id` was left out. The message lists the ids. |
| `other` | Any other error, such as a refused `start_session`. |

A tool in the full toolset raises its error as `[E0201] message`. A keyword with several fallback values fails with `All fallback values failed for keyword '…'` and the code of the last try.

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/http-api

# HTTP API reference

> Learn the endpoints `optics serve` exposes for starting sessions, running keywords and streaming results.

`optics serve` runs a local HTTP server that lets any language or tool drive a device through Optics. You start a session, send keywords one at a time, and read screenshots, UI trees and events back.

For a guided introduction, see [Drive Optics over HTTP](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/http-api). The machine-readable OpenAPI document is at [https://optics-framework.org/openapi.json](https://optics-framework.org/openapi.json).

## Start the server

```text
optics serve [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--workers N]
```

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. |
| `--port` | `8000` | The port to listen on. |
| `--workers` | `1` | Server processes. Keep it at 1. Sessions live in each process's memory, so with more workers a request can reach a process that doesn't know your session and get a 404. |

The server prints its own log lines and Optics' debug logs to the terminal. Interactive docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` while it runs.

**Warning:**
The API has no authentication. Anyone who can reach the port can control your devices. Keep the default `127.0.0.1`, or put the server behind a gateway that adds authentication. On another address, the server logs a warning when it starts.

Two more checks keep web pages away from the server:

- **CORS is off.** A web page cannot call the server, unless you list its origin in `OPTICS_CORS_ORIGINS`, such as `https://dash.example.com`. Separate origins with commas. The value `*` stops the server with E0501.
- **The Host header must be a loopback name.** On `127.0.0.1`, a request with another `Host`, such as a domain that points to `127.0.0.1`, gets `421 Misdirected Request`. To allow more names, or to apply the check on any address, list the names in `OPTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. Separate names with commas. Loopback names stay allowed.

In a container, publish the port on the host loopback and set `OPTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost`:

```shell
$ docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 -e OPTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost <image>
```

The server does not read config.yaml or the test files of your project. Each session gets its engines from the request. Sessions do not save screenshots or page sources, and they log at `DEBUG`. Each session writes its other output, such as `junit_output.xml`, to its own temporary folder. The server deletes the folder when the session stops.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/` or `/health` | Checks the server is up. Returns `{"status": "Optics Framework API is running", "version": "1.11.3"}`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/sessions/start` | Starts a session from a [SessionConfig](#sessionconfig) and launches the app. Returns `{"session_id", "driver_id", "status": "created"}`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/action` | Runs one keyword from an [ExecuteRequest](#executerequest). Returns `{"execution_id", "status": "SUCCESS", "data"}`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/templates` | Uploads an image template: `{"name", "image_base64"}`. The image can be raw base64 or a `data:` URL. Use the name as an element for the rest of the session. Returns `{"name", "status": "ok"}`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/api` | Replaces the session's API definitions for `Invoke API`. Send `{"api": {"collections": ...}}`. Returns 204. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/screenshot` | The current screen. `data.result` is a base64 PNG without a `data:` prefix, or `""` if the capture failed. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/driver-id` | The driver's own session id in `data.result`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/variables` | Every variable in the session: `{"variables": {"name": ["value", ...]}}`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/elements` | Elements on screen in `data.result`. Query: `filter_config` (`all`, `interactive`, `buttons`, `inputs`, `images`, `text`; repeatable) and `compact=true`. `compact` ignores the filter. Appium, Appium web and Playwright only. See [Compact elements](#compact-elements). |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/source` | The UI tree or HTML. `data` is `{"page_source", "timestamp"}` directly, not under `result`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/screen_elements` | A screenshot and its elements from the same frame. `data` is `{"screenshot", "elements"}` directly, not under `result`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/events` | A stream of keyword events. See [Streams](#streams). |
| `GET` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/stream` | A stream of screenshots and elements whenever the screen changes. See [Streams](#streams). |
| `GET` | `/v1/keywords` | Every keyword, including flow control. See [Keyword list](#keyword-list). |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/sessions/{id}/stop` | Closes the app and ends the session. Returns `{"status": "terminated"}`. |

### Compact elements

With `compact=true`, each element is one row:

```json
{"i": 1, "label": "Username", "cls": "input", "bounds": [494, 154, 786, 193], "act": ["tap", "input"], "rid": "user-name", "loc": "css=[data-test=\"username\"]"}
```

- `act` lists what the element accepts: `tap`, `long`, `toggle`, `input` or `scroll`. An empty list is read-only text.
- `rid` is the element's id, when it has one.
- `loc` is a locator that matches only this element. Use it as the element of a keyword.
- `offscreen: true` marks a web element that is on the page but scrolled out of view.

### Keyword list

Each item of `/v1/keywords` has the keyword's name, slug, description and parameters:

```json
{"keyword": "Get Text", "keyword_slug": "get_text", "description": "Get the text from a specified element. ...", "parameters": [{"name": "element", "type": "<class 'str'>", "default": null}, {"name": "index", "type": "<class 'str'>", "default": "0"}, ...], "returns": true, "deprecated": false}
```

`returns` is true when the keyword gives back a value. `deprecated` is true for a keyword you must not use in new tests, such as `Press Checkbox`.

## SessionConfig

The body of `POST /v1/sessions/start`. Every field is optional, but a session needs a driver and at least one element source.

| Field | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `driver_sources` | list | The driver. Each item is a name (`"playwright"`) or `{"appium": {"url": ..., "capabilities": {...}}}`. A listed item is enabled unless it says `"enabled": false`. |
| `elements_sources` | list | Element sources by name, for example `["appium_find_element", "appium_page_source", "appium_screenshot"]`. There's no default here, so always list them. |
| `text_detection` | list | OCR engines, for example `["easyocr"]`. |
| `image_detection` | list | Image engines, for example `["templatematch"]`. |
| `project_path` | string | Refused with `400` and E0501. Upload templates with `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/templates`. |
| `api_data` | object | API definitions for `Invoke API`, inline. File paths aren't supported. |
| `ai_self_heal` | boolean | Turns on [AI self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal). Defaults to `OPTICS_AI_SELF_HEAL`, else off. |
| `llm_provider` | string | The self-heal engine: `gemini`, `openai` or `anthropic`. Defaults to `OPTICS_LLM_PROVIDER`, else `gemini`. |
| `llm_model` | string | The self-heal model. Defaults to `OPTICS_LLM_MODEL`, else `gemini-2.5-flash` for Gemini. `openai` and `anthropic` need one. |
| `strict_element_match` | boolean | Accepts only exact text matches. |
| `appium_url`, `appium_config` | | Deprecated. Use `driver_sources`. |

Engine names are the same as in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#engine-lists). LLM credentials never go in the request, and neither does the server the `openai` engine calls. Set them in the server's environment (`OPENAI_BASE_URL` for the server). A session cannot set `api_key_env` or the `anthropic` `platform`, so each engine reads its default variables, such as `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and Claude runs on the Claude API. See [Environment variables](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#environment-variables).

The server does not read its own environment or files for a caller. It refuses these values with `400` and `E0501`:

- A `$NAME` or `${NAME}` reference in a driver `url` or in a `capabilities.headers` value. Send the value itself.
- A file path in `capabilities.storage_state`. Send the state as a JSON object.
- `capabilities.user_data_dir`. Set it in a project's config.yaml instead.
- `capabilities.profile`. A browser profile holds the sign-ins of the person who runs the server, so only a local stdio MCP server accepts it.
- `project_path`, and `credentials_path` in any capabilities.
- A `file:` URL, or another URL that opens a local resource of the browser, such as `chrome:`, `view-source:` or `about:` other than `about:blank`. This applies to `Launch App` and to each capability value, including a browser argument such as `--app=<url>`.
- `Read Data` from a file or from `ENV:`. Send the rows in the step instead.

```terminal
{"detail":{"type":"optics:config","code":"E0501","status":400,"message":"playwright: a browser profile works only through a local stdio MCP server","details":null,"meta":null,"cause":null}}
```

The session log shows only the scheme and host of a URL. It masks header values, `storage_state` and every value with a secret name, such as `token` or `password`.

## ExecuteRequest

The body of `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/action`.

| Field | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | Required. Must be `"keyword"`. |
| `keyword` | string | The keyword. `"Press Element"` and `"press_element"` both work. |
| `params` | list or object | Positional values as a list, or named values as an object: `{"element": "text=Sign in"}`. A value can be a list of strings: Optics tries each one until the keyword passes. |
| `template_images` | object | `{"name": "<base64>"}` images available to this request only. |

The session has no elements file, so pass locators directly, or define variables first with keywords such as `Evaluate`.

## Responses

A successful action returns:

```json
{
  "execution_id": "4f1c2b7e-...",
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "data": { "result": "Trail Runner 2" }
}
```

- When the keyword returns a value that isn't an object, `data` is `{"result": <value>}`.
- When the keyword returns an object, `data` is that object. This is why `/source` and `/screen_elements` put their fields directly in `data`.
- When self-heal recovers a step, `data` is `{"result", "healed": true, "heal_summary", "suggested_steps"}`. `suggested_steps` lists the keywords and parameters that fixed it.

Unlike `optics execute`, the HTTP API returns keyword results, so `Get Text`, `Assert Equality` and `Execute Script` values come back to you.

## Errors

| Status | When | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `mode` isn't `"keyword"`, a template image isn't valid base64, or `api_data` is invalid. | `{"detail": "<message>"}` |
| `400` | The request asks the server to read its own environment or files. See below. | A coded error with `E0501`. |
| `404` | The session doesn't exist. | `{"detail": "Session not found"}` |
| `404` | The keyword doesn't exist. | A coded error with `E0402`. |
| `4xx`/`5xx` | A keyword failed with an Optics error. The status comes from the code, for example `404` for `E0201`. | `{"detail": {"type", "code", "status", "message", "details", "meta", "cause"}}` |
| `500` | A keyword failed with an error that has no Optics code. | `{"detail": "Execution failed: <message>"}` |
| `500` | The session couldn't start. | `{"detail": "Session creation failed: ..."}` or a coded error. |

A keyword that does not find its element returns `404`:

```json
{"detail": {"type": "optics:element", "code": "E0201", "status": 404, "message": "No valid strategies found for 'css=#nope' in 'press_element'", "details": null, "meta": null, "cause": "E0201: Element 'css=#nope' not found."}}
```

- `cause` is the error that caused this one, or `null`.
- When you send several values for one parameter, Optics tries the next value only when the element is not found. It tries a maximum of 20 combinations. When each try fails, the message is `All <n> fallback combinations failed for keyword '<keyword>':` and lists the last five tries. The code and status are those of the last try.
- `Read Data` with a file or an `ENV:` path returns `400` with `E0501`.
- The `code` field holds the code alone, such as `E0402`. See [Error codes](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors).
- `DELETE /stop` on an unknown session returns 500 with `Session termination failed: 404: Session not found`.
- If closing the app fails during `DELETE /stop`, the session isn't removed. Call it again.

## Streams

Both stream endpoints use server-sent events (SSE): the connection stays open and each event is a `data:` line of JSON.

**`/events`** sends one event when each keyword starts, passes or fails, including the automatic `launch_app` at start, `close_and_terminate_app` at stop, and the GET helpers such as `/screenshot`.

```text
data: {"execution_id": "4f1c...", "status": "RUNNING", "message": "Starting keyword: press_element"}
data: {"execution_id": "4f1c...", "status": "SUCCESS", "message": "Keyword press_element executed successfully"}
```

- Statuses are `RUNNING`, `SUCCESS` and `FAIL`, plus `ERROR` or `CANCELLED` when the stream itself stops.
- After 15 seconds without events, it sends `{"execution_id": "heartbeat", "status": "HEARTBEAT", ...}`.
- Events wait in a queue until someone reads them. With several clients, each event goes to only one of them, so connect one client per session.

**`/workspace/stream`** sends the screen whenever it changes.

| Query | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `interval_ms` | `2000` | How often to check the screen. Minimum `500`. |
| `include_source` | `false` | Adds the UI tree or HTML as `source`. |
| `filter_config` | | Filters the elements, as for `/elements`. |

Each event is `{"screenshot", "elements", "screenshotFailed"}`, plus `source` when requested. It's sent only when the screen or elements change. Otherwise a `{"type": "heartbeat"}` arrives every 15 seconds, and errors arrive as `{"type": "error", "message"}`. The stream ends when the session ends.

## Walkthrough

This drives the Birch app on an Android emulator. You need an Appium server on port 4723 and the `appium` extra.

### Start the server

```shell
$ optics serve --port 8000
```

Leave it running and open a second terminal.

### Start a session

```shell
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/start \
>   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
>   -d '{"driver_sources": [{"appium": {"url": "http://127.0.0.1:4723",
>          "capabilities": {"platformName": "Android", "automationName": "UiAutomator2",
>            "deviceName": "emulator-5554", "appPackage": "com.birch.shop",
>            "appActivity": "com.birch.shop.MainActivity"}}}],
>        "elements_sources": ["appium_find_element", "appium_page_source", "appium_screenshot"],
>        "text_detection": [], "image_detection": []}'
{"session_id":"8d0e7c55-...","driver_id":"...","status":"created"}
```

The app launches. Save the session id:

```shell
$ SID=8d0e7c55-...
```

### Watch events (optional)

In a third terminal:

```shell
$ curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/events
```

### Run keywords

```shell
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/action \
>   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
>   -d '{"mode": "keyword", "keyword": "Press Element", "params": [["//*[@resource-id=\"com.birch.shop:id/search\"]", "text=Search"]]}'
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/action \
>   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
>   -d '{"mode": "keyword", "keyword": "Enter Text", "params": {"element": "text=Search", "text": "Trail Runner 2"}}'
$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/action \
>   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
>   -d '{"mode": "keyword", "keyword": "Assert Presence", "params": ["text=Trail Runner 2", "20"]}'
```

The first call passes a list for `element`, so Optics tries the XPath and then the text.

### Save a screenshot

```shell
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/screenshot \
>   | python3 -c 'import sys,json,base64; open("screen.png","wb").write(base64.b64decode(json.load(sys.stdin)["data"]["result"]))'
```

### End the session

```shell
$ curl -s -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/sessions/$SID/stop
{"status":"terminated"}
```

Optics writes `junit_output.xml` for the session to the temporary folder of the session. The server deletes the folder when the session stops.

## Limits

- Sessions live in memory. `optics live` and `optics mcp` cannot see them. When the server stops, it ends every session and closes its drivers.
- There's no record or save endpoint. Write the steps you ran into [project files](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files) to replay them with `optics execute`.
- Error detection doesn't run over HTTP.
- With the `ble` driver, the automatic `launch_app` at session start fails, because BLE can't launch apps.

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors

# Error codes

> Learn what each Optics error code means and how to fix it.

When a step or command fails, Optics usually attaches a code such as `E0201`. The code tells you which part of Optics failed, and the message after it says why. This page lists every code in Optics 1.11.3 and what to do about each one.

## How codes are built

A code is a letter followed by four digits.

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| First letter | `E` is an error. `X` is an error after Optics tried every fallback or caught an exception. `W` is a warning. |
| First two digits | The family: `01` driver, `02` elements, `03` screenshots, `04` keywords, `05` files and config, `06` engines and modules, `07` test cases and variables, `08` general, `09` `optics live`. |
| Last two digits | The specific problem in that family. |

Codes in the `E02` family and `X0201` mean "element not found". When a step uses an element with fallback values, only these codes make Optics try the next value. Any other code fails the step straight away.

## Where codes appear

| Where | What it looks like |
|---|---|
| `optics execute` "Failure details" box | `<test> → step '<step>' — Keyword '<keyword>' failed: E0401: <message>`, with ` (cause: <cause>)` at the end when there is a deeper cause |
| Log files (`file_log: true`) | The same reason as the Failure details box, as an error line in `execution_logs.log`. A deeper cause follows as ` caused by: <cause>`. |
| Error panels | A red panel with the code as its title. A deeper cause shows on a `Caused by:` line. |
| `optics live` history | `✗ press_element ${sign_in}` with `[E0201] ...` on the line below |
| HTTP API (`optics serve`) | A `code` field in the error body, or the code inside a `detail` string. A `cause` field holds the deeper cause. See [HTTP API](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/http-api#errors). |
| JUnit report (`junit_output.xml`) | A `code` attribute on each `<failure>`, `<error>` and failed `<kw>`. See [Read results](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results#read-the-junit-report). |
| MCP server (`optics mcp`) | `[E0201] not found: ...` in the tool reply, with a `Next:` line and the current screen rows. See [MCP server](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp#errors). |

The cause is the innermost error of the chain, on one line of at most 300 characters. Optics leaves it out when the message already contains it.

Not every failure has a code. See [Messages without a code](#messages-without-a-code).

## E01: Driver and session

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0101` | **Driver not initialized.** A keyword ran before the driver session started. In `optics live` this happens when the automatic `launch_app` failed. | Start with `Launch App`. In `optics live`, run `launch_app` again and read its error first. |
| `E0102` | **Failed to start session.** The driver couldn't create a session. The Appium server refused it, Playwright couldn't open or connect to the browser, or the request took too long. On Playwright, each call has a limit of `action_timeout_ms` (15 seconds). Launch App can take up to `connect_timeout_ms` + `navigation_timeout_ms` + `action_timeout_ms` (165 seconds). | Check that the server is running and the device is connected with `optics doctor <folder>`. Check the capabilities, especially `appPackage`, `appActivity` or `bundleId`. Read the Appium server's own log for the cause. For a remote browser, check the `url` and `headers`. Raise the [Playwright timeouts](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#playwright-capabilities) for slow pages. |
| `E0104` | **Driver config incomplete.** A required driver setting is missing or wrong: empty Appium `capabilities`, no `platformName`, an unsupported `platformName`, or no server `url`. Also raised when `Press Keycode` gets a remote key name that a Samsung or LG TV does not know (`Unknown remote key '<name>' for <TV>. Known keys: ...`). The message lists the names that work. Also raised when `Get App Version` gets a name that is not an Android package name, such as `com.example.app`. | Fill in the driver settings in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#examples-by-platform). `platformName` must be `Android`, `iOS`, `TizenTV` or `LGTV`. For a TV key, use a name from [Move around with remote keys](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/tv#move-around-with-remote-keys). |
| `E0105` | **Keyword not supported on this device platform.** You used a keyword on a Samsung or LG TV that needs a touch screen: a coordinate tap, a swipe, a scroll, `Select Dropdown Option`, the `checked` state of `Is Element`, typing without an element, or `Go Back`. Also raised by `Enter Text` with a special key that an app keyboard does not have, such as `<tab>`. Also raised by `Go Back` on a driver without it (`'go_back' is not supported by the <Driver> driver.`) and by a special key that Playwright cannot map. | Move the focus with `Press Element`, or press a remote key with `Press Keycode`, such as `UP`, `DOWN`, `ENTER` or `BACK`. See [Test TV apps](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/tv#keywords-that-fail-on-tizen-and-webos). |
| `E0106` | **Driver session is no longer active.** The Appium or Selenium server dropped the session, for example after a timeout, a device disconnect or a server restart. A refused connection to the server in the middle of a run also counts. Optics doesn't reconnect. Also raised when Appium cannot go back to the app after it read a web page. In `optics execute`, a keyword with this error ends as `ERROR`, not `FAIL`, and its test case does the same. | Run the tests again. Over HTTP or MCP, end the session and start a new one. If it keeps happening, raise `newCommandTimeout` in the capabilities. |

## E02: Elements

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0201` | **Element not found.** No strategy found the element on the current screen. Also raised when a `${name}` variable isn't defined, when OCR is needed but no `text_detection` engine is enabled, or when `Scroll Until Element Appears` or `Swipe Until Element Appears` time out. On web pages it also means: `'<element>' is covered by another element on the page.`, `'<element>' is in the page but not displayed.`, `'<element>' matched N web element(s); index i is out of range.`, `Cannot read the web page shown by '<app>'` or `Cannot place the web element: its centre is outside the web view that shows the page.` | Check the locator against the screen with `optics live` or the page source. Put `Assert Presence` before the step if the element appears late. Playwright actions wait up to `element_timeout_ms` (10 seconds), but other drivers do not wait. Add fallback values in `Element_ID_*` columns. Enable `easyocr` if you locate by visible text. |
| `X0201` | **Element not found after all fallbacks.** Optics found the element, or tried every fallback value, but the action failed each time. The element may be hidden, covered, disabled, or the wrong match. | Use `index` to pick the right match, an [area of interest](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/area-of-interest) to narrow the search, or a more specific locator. Turn on [AI self-heal](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/self-heal) for popups that get in the way. |
| `E0202` | **Unsupported operation for element source.** The enabled element sources can't do what the keyword asked, usually listing interactive elements. | Enable `appium_page_source` or `playwright_page_source`. Selenium can't list interactive elements; use the page source instead. |
| `E0205` | **Invalid element type.** An area of interest is out of range, or a `rule` isn't `any` or `all`. | Keep area values between 0 and 100, with `aoi_x + aoi_width` and `aoi_y + aoi_height` at most 100. Set `rule` to `any` or `all`. |

## E03: Screenshots

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0303` | **Screenshot empty or black.** Optics couldn't take a screenshot, got a black image, or has no screenshot source enabled. Also raised when `appium_screenshot` runs on a Samsung Tizen TV: `This TV cannot take a screenshot through Appium; use camera_screenshot`. | Enable the screenshot source for your driver, such as `appium_screenshot`. Check that the device screen is on and unlocked. Some apps block screenshots on secure screens. For a Tizen TV, use `camera_screenshot`. See [BLE and camera](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#ble-and-camera). |
| `E0304` | **Image too large to decode or not a valid image.** An image is not PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP or TIFF, or it is larger than 64 MiB or 67,108,864 pixels. Examples are a template upload over HTTP and a camera frame. | Send a smaller image in one of these formats. For a camera, lower the resolution of the frame server. |

## E04: Keywords and parameters

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0401` | **Action failed.** The keyword ran but couldn't complete: an app didn't launch, an element wasn't visible or enabled for `Is Element`, typing failed, a script failed, an API request failed, or a module run by `Run Loop`, `Condition` or `Execute Module` failed. Also raised when `Assert Text` finds other text (`Element '<element>' shows '<text>' but expected '<expected>'.`), when `Assert Equality` finds two different values (`Expected '<expected>', got '<actual>'.`), when `Is Element` finds the wrong state or finds the element only by OCR or image, when iOS `Go Back` finds no back button, or when a deep link does not open. In `optics live`, also shown for errors a keyword logged without failing. | Read the message after the code; it names the cause. For nested modules, the inner error is included. |
| `X0401` | **Action failed with exception.** A keyword failed with an error that has no Optics code. The JUnit report gives this code to the failed step. | Read the message of the `<failure>`. |
| `E0402` | **Keyword not found.** No keyword has that name. | Check the spelling with `optics list`. Case and spaces don't matter. |
| `E0403` | **Invalid keyword parameters.** A parameter has the wrong form: an expression that can't be evaluated, a numeric comparison on string values, a bad loop count, a query that matches no data, an `Invoke API` id without a dot, an `Invoke API` response that is not JSON, a key name that Playwright does not know. Also raised for an unknown `${name}` inside a longer value (`Variable '${name}' in '<value>' is not defined.`), for a `store_as` with no name or no value to store, or when the page source can't be read. Also raised for a number out of range: `'repeat' must be a number from 1 to 100, got '<value>'`. Pixel coordinates and lengths go from 0 to 16,384, and percentages from 0 to 100. Over HTTP and MCP, also raised for too many positional parameters. | Read the message. In `Condition` and `Evaluate`, compare with quoted values: `${size} == '9'`, not `${size} > 5`. Use `collection.api` for `Invoke API`. Write `store_as=<name>` only on a keyword that returns a value. See [Keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/). |
| `E0405` | **Action ran, but the screen does not show its result.** The action ran, but the check after it failed. On a Samsung or LG TV, `Enter Text` types on the on-screen keyboard and then reads the field. The error shows when the field does not show the text or typing stopped part way. It also shows when `Clear Element Text` leaves text in the field. No fallback value runs the action again, because the action already ran. In `optics mcp`, this error has the kind `silent_failure`. | Read the message. Check the field on the TV. Press the field with `Press Element` first when the screen has more than one field. Then run the step again. See [Type on a TV](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/tv#type-on-a-tv). |
| `E0406` | **Expression or filter refused.** An `Evaluate`, `Condition` or `Read Data` expression uses something other than values, names, arithmetic, comparisons, `in`, `and`, `or` and `not`. Function calls and the pandas operators `&`, `\|` and `~` are refused. Also raised for an expression that is too large to compute, such as `2**10**10`. | Remove the function call, or compute the value in an earlier step. In a `Read Data` filter, write `and`, `or` and `not`. See [Flow control keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/flow). |

## E05: Files and config

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0501` | **Missing required files.** A file, folder or setting Optics needs isn't there: the project folder doesn't exist, no driver or element source is enabled, a `Read Data` file or `ENV:` variable is missing, a CSV is empty, or config.yaml can't be parsed. Also raised for a Playwright setting that is not valid (`device`, `storage_state`, `protocol`, `context`), for an environment variable in `url` or `headers` that is not set (`Environment variable NAME is not set`), and when `optics serve` or `optics mcp` get `${NAME}`, a `storage_state` path or `Read Data` with `ENV:`. Also raised for a Chrome or Edge `profile` that matches none or more than one (`No browser profile '<name>'. Profiles: ...`). Also raised for `profile` and `user_data_dir` set together, for a `profile` over HTTP, `optics serve` or a remote `url`, and for `user_data_dir` in an API session. Also raised for a `credentials_path` file that is missing or is not a Google service account key. Also raised for a `$NAME` or `${NAME}` in config.yaml when the environment variable is not set or is empty, and for a `./` path in config.yaml that does not exist. `optics serve` and `optics mcp` over HTTP also raise it for `project_path`, `credentials_path`, a `file:` URL and a `Read Data` file, and `optics serve` for `OPTICS_CORS_ORIGINS=*`. In `optics live`, also raised by `/save` with nothing recorded and by plain-English mode with no LLM engine enabled. | Check the path or setting in the message. Set the environment variable before the run. For a profile, pick one from the list in the message. See [Start signed in with a browser profile](https://optics-framework.org/docs/platforms/web#start-signed-in-with-a-browser-profile). Run `optics doctor <folder>` to check config.yaml. Enable one driver and its element sources. |
| `E0503` | **Config parser error.** A config list or API file has the wrong shape, or a YAML file can't be parsed. Also raised for an empty `--include` or `--exclude` name. Also raised when two test cases have the same setup or teardown role: `The test cases have more than one test setup: '<first>' and '<second>'`. | Write each engine as a list item with a name: `- appium: {enabled: true, ...}`. Check YAML indentation. See [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#engine-lists) and [API definitions](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files#api-definitions). For two setups, keep one name that ends with "Setup" and rename the other. See [Setup and teardown](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files#setup-and-teardown). |

## E06: Modules and engines

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0601` | **Module not found.** One of: an enabled engine name doesn't exist, or its extra isn't installed (for example `openai` without the `openai` extra), or an `openai` or `anthropic` engine has no `model` or key, or has a `timeout_s`, `response_format` or `platform` that is not valid, or its client cannot start; `Execute Module`, `Run Loop` or `Condition` names a module that doesn't exist; `Invoke API` names an unknown collection or API; or `--runner` has an unknown value. | Check the name in the message. Install the extra with `optics setup --install <name>`. Check module names against modules.csv, including case and spaces. |
| `E0603` | **Factory init failed.** The name under an engine key matches a file inside Optics, but that file isn't an engine of that kind, for example a helper module's name. | Use one of the names listed for that key in [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#engine-lists) or [Engines and extras](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines). |

## E07: Test cases and variables

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0701` | **Execution failed.** A run or a session action failed and Optics wrapped the cause. Also raised when the run order can't be built. | Read the wrapped message after `Execution failed:`. |
| `E0702` | **Test case not found.** No test cases were loaded, an HTTP session no longer exists, or a variable used in `Evaluate`, `Condition` or a `Read Data` query isn't defined. Also raised when an `include` or `exclude` name matches no test case, matches only setup or teardown test cases, or leaves no test case to run. In `optics live`, also raised when the session can't start or switch devices. | Check that your test cases file is found (see [Project files](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files#how-optics-finds-your-files)). Define the variable in elements.csv or create it in an earlier step. Fix the test case names that the message shows. |
| `E0706` | **Run stopped before the test case finished.** You pressed Ctrl+C, or Optics received SIGTERM. The report gives this code to the test case and the keyword that were in progress. | Run the tests again. |

## E08: General

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0801` | **Unexpected error.** The LLM request failed, the model refused it, the model returned a reply Optics couldn't read, the reply hit the output limit, or a keyword produced no result and no error. | Check your LLM key, model name and quota. If the message names `max_tokens`, raise `capabilities.max_tokens`. Retry the step. If it repeats, rerun with `log_level: DEBUG` and report it. |

## E09: optics live

| Code | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `E0901` | **Named element not defined in this project.** You typed `${name}` in `optics live`, and no elements file defines it. | Add the name to elements.csv, or type the locator directly. Use `/elements` to see the names Optics found. |

## Reserved codes

These codes exist in Optics 1.11.3, but nothing raises them. If you see one, it came from a newer version or your own code.

| Code | Default message |
|---|---|
| `E0103` | Failed to end session |
| `W0104` | Driver config incomplete (warning) |
| `W0203` | Element format mismatch |
| `E0204` | Timeout locating element |
| `E0301` | Screenshot disabled |
| `W0302` | Fallback to next camera supported driver |
| `W0404` | Keyword deprecated |
| `X0502` | File read exception |
| `W0503` | Config parser warning (can be ignored) |
| `W0602` | No valid instances, ignoring it |
| `X0604` | Import related problem |
| `E0703` | Parameter resolution failed |
| `E0704` | Test case timeout |
| `W0705` | Test case skipped |
| `E0802` | Unhandled exception |

## Messages without a code

These common `optics execute` and `optics dry_run` failures have no code.

| Message | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `Keyword not found: <name>. Did you mean '<keyword>'?` | A module step names a keyword that doesn't exist. | Fix the spelling. Run `optics list` to see every keyword. |
| `Unknown keyword or module: '<name>'` | A test step names neither a module nor a keyword. | Check the module name in modules.csv, including case. |
| `Element not found: <name>` | A step uses `${name}`, and no elements file defines it. | Add the name to elements.csv, or create it in an earlier step. |
| `Keyword '<name>' failed after fallback attempts; last error: <error>` | Every fallback value of the element failed. | Check each value in the element's row. See `E0201` and `X0201` above. |
| `API '<name>' returned status 200, expected 404.` | An `Invoke API` call got another HTTP status than `expected_status`. | Check the status in the API definition. See [Invoke API](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/flow#invoke-api). |
| `Missing required files in <folder>: test_cases, modules` | Optics found no test cases file or no modules file. | Check the header rows. See [Project files](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files). |
| `No driver enabled in <folder>/config.yaml` | A module that the run reaches uses an action, app or verification keyword, and no `driver_sources` entry has `enabled: true`. The panel title is `Cannot start: E0104`. A suite of flow control keywords needs no driver. | Run `optics configure <folder>`, or `optics doctor <folder>` to find the problem. |
| `Cannot start` panel | The preflight couldn't reach the Appium or Selenium server, or found no Android device. Also shown for `include` or `exclude` names that are not valid. | Follow the command in the panel, for example start `appium`. Set `OPTICS_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1` to skip the check. For test case names, see [Pick test cases](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#pick-test-cases). |

Plain Python errors, such as `ValueError: invalid literal for int()` when a timeout is `2.5`, also fail a step without a code. Timeouts and counts must be whole numbers. See [Troubleshooting](https://optics-framework.org/docs/help/troubleshooting).

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/help/

# Get help

> Find the answer to a problem yourself, or report it so someone else can.

Most problems have a known fix. Start with the pages below, and ask on GitHub when they don't cover your case.

- [Troubleshooting](https://optics-framework.org/docs/help/troubleshooting): Fixes for common install, setup and run problems, listed by the message you see.
- [FAQ](https://optics-framework.org/docs/help/faq): Short answers about what Optics does, what it doesn't, and why.
- [Glossary](https://optics-framework.org/docs/help/glossary): Every term the docs use, in one place.

## Where to look first

Run `optics doctor` on your project before anything else. It checks Python, every engine, the Appium server, connected devices and your `config.yaml`, and prints the fix next to each problem:

```shell
$ optics doctor my-project
```

Always pass the project folder. Without it, doctor checks your machine but not your config. If doctor shows no ❌ rows and the problem remains:

1. **Search [Troubleshooting](https://optics-framework.org/docs/help/troubleshooting) for the exact message.** Problems are listed by the words Optics prints, such as `No driver enabled` or `Element not found`.
2. **Look up the code.** If the message has a code like `E0201`, [Error codes](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors) says what it means and what to do.
3. **Read the [FAQ](https://optics-framework.org/docs/help/faq)** when something works differently from what you expected. Some behavior is a known limit, not a bug.

## Ask a question or report a bug

Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/mozarkai/optics-framework/issues). Search the open and closed issues first, since someone may have hit the same problem.

A good report lets someone reproduce the problem without asking you anything. Include:

- **Your Optics version.** Run `optics --version`.
- **The `optics doctor` output for your project.** Run `optics doctor <project>` and paste everything it prints.
- **Your `config.yaml`, without secrets.** Remove API keys, passwords and tokens, and replace private URLs with placeholders.
- **The failing step.** Paste the rows from `modules/modules.csv` and `test_data/elements.csv` that the step uses, and the full "Failure details" box from the run.
- **The log.** Choose the one that matches what you ran:
  - `optics execute`: set `file_log: true` in `config.yaml`, run again, and attach `execution_output/internal_logs.log` and `execution_output/execution_logs.log`. Set `log_level: DEBUG` for the most detail.
  - `optics live`: attach `logs/optics_live_<time>.log` from the project folder. Its path is printed when you quit.
- **What you expected, and what happened instead.** A screenshot from `execution_output/` often shows the difference at a glance.

**Warning:**
Logs and screenshots can contain personal data, such as names and email addresses on screen. Check them before you attach them to a public issue. Values written with the `@:` prefix are masked as `****` in log files, but screenshots show whatever was on screen.

## Report a security issue

Don't open a public issue for a security problem. Report it privately, as described in the repository's [security policy](https://github.com/mozarkai/optics-framework/security/policy).

---

Source: https://optics-framework.org/docs/help/troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

> Fix the most common problems with installing, configuring and running Optics.

Problems are grouped by when they happen and named by the message Optics prints, so you can search this page for the words on your screen. Start with `optics doctor <project>`, which finds many of these for you. For messages with a code such as `E0201`, see [Error codes](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors).

## Installing

### `optics: command not found`

Your shell can't find the `optics` command. The installer adds it to your PATH, but only new terminals pick that up.

Open a new terminal. If it still fails, add `~/.optics/bin` to your PATH, as the installer printed. With pip, activate the virtual environment you installed into.

### Optics needs Python 3.12 or newer

Optics runs on Python 3.12 and later. pip on an older Python reports that no matching version of `optics-framework` exists.

Check with `python3 --version`, then install a current Python from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) or use the installer, which sets up its own environment. See [Install Optics](https://optics-framework.org/docs/get-started/install).

### "Cannot start": Optics could not load one of its dependencies

Every command stops with a red panel because a package Optics needs is missing or broken. This usually follows a partial upgrade or a package installed into the wrong environment.

Run the reinstall command shown in the panel, for example `pip install --force-reinstall optics-framework`. It matches the way you installed Optics.

### `optics setup` refuses to install

`optics setup` and `optics quickstart` won't install engines into environments that another tool manages: Conda, pipx, `uv tool`, and project environments run by uv, Poetry, PDM or Pipenv. They also refuse a system Python marked as externally managed.

Run the command the message suggests, such as `pipx inject optics-framework …` or `poetry add …`. Or install Optics into a plain virtual environment, where `optics setup` works. See [Where installs are refused](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/engines#where-installs-are-refused).

### EasyOCR fails under Conda

EasyOCR and Optics need different major versions of NumPy under Conda, so they can't share a Conda environment.

Use the installer or a standard `venv` instead of Conda.

### The MCP server isn't installed by `optics setup`

`optics setup --install mcp` reports `Invalid engine(s): mcp`, and the `all` bundle leaves the MCP server out.

The install scripts include it. With pip, install it yourself: `pip install "optics-framework[mcp]"`. See [MCP server](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/mcp#install).

## Setting up a project

### "Cannot start: E0104": No driver enabled in …/config.yaml

No entry under `driver_sources` has `enabled: true`, and the test cases use a keyword that needs a driver. Optics also prints this when it could not read `config.yaml` at all, for example because of a YAML syntax error or a value of the wrong type, and fell back to defaults. A suite that uses only [flow control keywords](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/flow) needs no driver.

- Run `optics doctor <project>`. Its `config: file` row shows whether the file parses.
- Set `enabled: true` on one driver, or run `optics configure <project>` to write a working config.
- Check indentation: each engine is a list item, as in `- appium:` followed by its settings indented below.

### "Cannot start: E0501": Missing required files in …: test_cases, modules

Optics finds files by their header row, not their names, and found no test cases file or no modules file.

Check the first line of each file: `test_case,test_step` for test cases and `module_name,module_step,param_1,…` for modules. Case does not matter. A spreadsheet app can add an invisible character to the first cell when it saves as "CSV UTF-8", so save as plain CSV. See [How Optics finds your files](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/files#how-optics-finds-your-files).

### "Cannot start: E0102": No Appium server reachable at …

Before a run, `optics execute` checks that the Appium server answers at the `url` in `config.yaml`. Nothing is listening there. The report `junit_output.xml` shows each test case as `ERROR` with the same message.

Start the server in another terminal with `appium`, then run again. If the server runs on another port or machine, fix `url` under `driver_sources`. On Android, the same panel appears when `adb` isn't installed or no device is connected; check with `adb devices`.

### "Cannot start: E0102": No Selenium/WebDriver server reachable at …

No Selenium server answers at the `url` in `config.yaml`. The report `junit_output.xml` shows each test case as `ERROR` with the same message.

Start one, for example with Docker: `docker run -d -p 4444:4444 selenium/standalone-chrome`. Check that `url` in `config.yaml` points to it, usually `http://localhost:4444/wd/hub`.

### "Selenium capabilities not found in config"

The Selenium driver needs a `browserName` under `capabilities`. `optics configure` writes `capabilities: {}` for Selenium, which can't start, and `optics doctor` doesn't catch it.

Add `browserName: chrome` or `browserName: firefox` under `capabilities`. Those are the only two browsers the Selenium driver supports. See [config.yaml examples](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#examples-by-platform).

### `E0104` Appium capabilities not found or unsupported platform

The Appium driver needs non-empty `capabilities` with a `platformName` of `Android`, `iOS`, `TizenTV` or `LGTV`.

Fill in the capabilities for your platform. Run `optics configure <project>` to answer a few questions instead of writing them by hand. See [Error codes](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e01-driver-and-session).

### YAML test cases load nothing

A YAML file with `test_cases:` at the top is recognized as a test cases file but loads no tests. The run then stops with "Cannot start: E0702" and the text "No test cases to run". Section names in YAML suites are exact.

Use `Test Cases:`, `Modules:` and `Elements:`, with that capitalization and spacing. See [Section names are exact](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/yaml#section-names-are-exact).

### My config.yaml changes have no effect

Optics ignores keys it doesn't know, so a typo such as `driver_source` is skipped without a warning. If your project folder holds more than one YAML file with `driver_sources` and `elements_sources`, `optics execute` uses the last one it finds, which may not be the one you edited.

Check the spelling against [config.yaml](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/config#top-level-keys). Keep one config file per project; to switch targets, copy a different file into place. See [Run the same suite on different devices](https://optics-framework.org/docs/create/organise#run-the-same-suite-on-different-devices).

## Finding elements

### "Element not found: <name>"

A step uses `${name}`, and no elements file defines `name`. The step fails before Optics looks at the screen.

- Add a row for `name` to `test_data/elements.csv`, and check the spelling and case.
- If an `Invoke API` `extract` creates the value, add a placeholder row (`access_token,placeholder`) so `optics dry_run` accepts it. Other keywords that write a variable need no row. See [Dry runs](https://optics-framework.org/docs/advanced/variables#dry-runs).
- If every name fails, check that the elements file starts with `Element_Name,Element_ID` and that you saved it as plain CSV.

### `[E0201]` No valid strategies found

Optics looked for the element every way it could and didn't find it on the current screen.

- Check the value against the screen. In `optics live`, try it with `assert_presence` and see whether it's found.
- If the element appears late, put `Assert Presence` before the step. Actions don't wait.
- For text drawn inside images, enable a [text detection engine](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/text-and-images#turn-on-ocr) and a screenshot source.
- Add fallback values, so a second way can take over when the first breaks.
- Open `execution_output/failed_steps_elements.json`. It lists the elements that were on screen when the step failed.

See [`E0201` and `X0201`](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/errors#e02-elements).

### "OCR was not tried: no text_detection engine is configured"

The step did not find the element in the UI tree. Optics did not read the screenshot, because no OCR engine is enabled.

If the text is in the UI tree, fix the value. If the text is drawn inside an image, [turn on OCR](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/text-and-images#turn-on-ocr).

### A text value is treated as an XPath or CSS selector

Optics decides what a value is from how it looks. Text that starts with `(` or `/`, or contains `[` and `]`, is read as an XPath or CSS selector: `(optional)`, `Price [USD]`, `.com`.

Put `text=` in front to force text, for example `text=(optional)`. See [Choose the kind of value](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/define#choose-the-kind-of-value).

### `id:` values always fail

No element source supports values written as `id:login`, so they fail with `E0201` every time.

Use an XPath on the id instead, for example `//*[@resource-id='com.birch.shop:id/login']` on Android or `//*[@id='login']` on the web.

### Assert Presence with several elements fails

Assert Presence, Assert Visibility and Validate Screen separate elements with `|`, not commas. In a CSV, a comma starts a new cell, so the second element becomes the timeout and the step fails with `ValueError: invalid literal for int()`.

Write `Assert Presence,Welcome|Picked for you,20`. See [Check several elements at once](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/verification#check-several-elements-at-once).

### Images aren't found

Image values refer to a picture by file name, and Optics searches the whole project folder for it.

- Use the file name only (`cart_icon.png`), not a path.
- Keep the picture inside the project folder, and give every picture a unique file name. Two files with the same name in different folders replace each other.
- Use `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.bmp`. Other formats aren't treated as images.
- Enable `templatematch` under `image_detection` and a screenshot source under `elements_sources`.

See [Capture a good template](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/text-and-images#capture-a-good-template).

### OCR is slow on the first run

EasyOCR downloads its models the first time it runs, and loads them at the start of every run. The first run can take minutes on a slow connection.

Let the first run finish once; later runs reuse the download. To make OCR faster in general, list UI tree sources before screenshot sources and use an [area of interest](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/area-of-interest). See [Speed things up](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/text-and-images#speed-things-up).

### The wrong match is tapped

The same text or picture appears more than once on screen, and Optics took the first match.

Add `index=1` to pick the second match, counting from 0, or narrow the search with an [area of interest](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/area-of-interest). See [Pick one of several matches](https://optics-framework.org/docs/elements/define#pick-one-of-several-matches).

## Running tests

### "Keyword not found: X. Did you mean …"

A module step names a keyword that doesn't exist, usually because of a typo. Optics suggests the closest real name.

Fix the spelling. Case and spaces don't matter, so `Press Element` and `press element` both work. Run `optics list` to see every keyword.

### A module that calls another module reports "Keyword not found"

A module step that names another module is read as a keyword name.

Call the other module with `Execute Module`: `Checkout,Execute Module,Sign In`. See [Execute Module](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/keywords/flow#execute-module).

### "Cannot start: E0702": include matches no test case

A name in `--include`, `--exclude` or the `include` and `exclude` lists of `config.yaml` matches no test case. Optics also stops when no test case is left to run. The exit code is `3`, and Optics writes no report.

Read the suggestion and the list of available test cases in the panel. Matching ignores case and uses `*` and `?` as wildcards. See [Pick test cases](https://optics-framework.org/docs/reference/cli#pick-test-cases).

### The run stopped, and the report shows ERROR and NOT_RUN

Someone pressed Ctrl+C (exit code `130`), or the CI system sent SIGTERM (exit code `143`). Optics stops at once and still writes `junit_output.xml`. The test case in progress is `ERROR`. The test cases that did not start, and Suite Teardown, are `NOT_RUN`.

Run the suite again. A CI job that you cancel on purpose gives the same result. See [What each outcome writes](https://optics-framework.org/docs/run/results#what-each-outcome-writes).
